    75	
    76	### Choosing a path
    77	
    78	- **Rust** gives native performance without a Python runtime. All core
    79	  trading functionality is available. Use it for latency-sensitive
    80	  deployments or teams that prefer a compiled language.
    81	- **Python** keeps the Python authoring experience. User components (actors,
    82	  strategies) run on the Rust core for data processing and execution.
    83	
    84	## Project setup
    85	
    86	The Nautilus crates are published to
    87	[crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/nautilus-backtest). Add them to your
    88	`Cargo.toml`:
    89	
    90	```toml
    91	[dependencies]
    92	nautilus-backtest = "0.63"
    93	nautilus-common = "0.63"
    94	nautilus-execution = "0.63"
    95	nautilus-model = { version = "0.63", features = ["test-support"] }
    96	nautilus-trading = { version = "0.63", features = ["examples"] }
    97	
    98	anyhow = "1"
    99	log = "0.4"
   100	```
   101	
   102	For live trading, add the live crate and the adapter for your venue:
   103	
   104	```toml
   105	[dependencies]
   106	nautilus-live = "0.63"
   107	nautilus-okx = "0.63"
   108	```
   109	
   110	To track the latest development branch, point all Nautilus dependencies at the
   111	same git source to avoid type mismatches between crates.io and git versions:
   112	
   113	```toml
   114	[dependencies]
   115	nautilus-backtest = { git = "https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader.git", branch = "develop" }
   116	nautilus-common = { git = "https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader.git", branch = "develop" }
   117	nautilus-execution = { git = "https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader.git", branch = "develop" }
   118	nautilus-model = { git = "https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader.git", branch = "develop", features = ["test-support"] }
   119	nautilus-trading = { git = "https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader.git", branch = "develop", features = ["examples"] }
   120	```
   121	
   122	The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is **1.98.1**.
   123	
   124	### Feature flags
   125	
   126	| Flag             | Crate               | Effect                                              |
   127	| ---------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
   128	| `high-precision` | `nautilus-model`    | 16-digit fixed precision (default is 9).            |
   129	| `test-support`   | `nautilus-model`    | Test fixtures, builders, specs, and defaults.       |
   130	| `examples`       | `nautilus-trading`  | Example strategies (`EmaCross`, `GridMarketMaker`). |
   131	| `streaming`      | `nautilus-backtest` | Catalog-based data streaming via `BacktestNode`.    |
   132	| `defi`           | `nautilus-model`    | DeFi data types. Implies `high-precision`.          |
   133	
   134	:::tip
   135	Standard 9-digit precision handles most traditional finance instruments.
   136	Enable `high-precision` for crypto venues where prices or quantities need more than nine decimal
   137	places.
   138	:::
   139	
   140	### Memory allocator
   141	
   142	The `nautilus` CLI and Python wheels use [mimalloc](https://crates.io/crates/mimalloc) for Rust
   143	allocations. A Rust binary chooses its own allocator, so add mimalloc to yours to match:
   144	
   145	```toml
   146	[dependencies]
   147	mimalloc = "0.1"
   148	```
   149	
   150	```rust
   151	use mimalloc::MiMalloc;
   152	use nautilus_common::logging::headers::register_allocator_mimalloc;
   153	
   154	#[global_allocator]
   155	static GLOBAL: MiMalloc = MiMalloc;
   156	
   157	fn main() {
   158	    register_allocator_mimalloc();
   159	}
   160	```
   161	
   162	Declaring `GLOBAL` selects mimalloc. Call `register_allocator_mimalloc` at the start of `main`,
   163	before constructing a Nautilus node, so the version header reports `allocator: mimalloc <version>`.
   164	Registration **only updates the header metadata**; it does not select the allocator.
   165	
   166	The default system allocator also works. Measure throughput and resident memory on your workload
   167	and platform when comparing allocator choices.
   168	See the [architecture guide](architecture.md#memory-allocation) for background.
   169	
   170	## Actors
   171	
   172	An actor receives market data, custom data/signals, and system events but does
   173	not manage orders. Implement the `DataActor` trait and use `nautilus_actor!` to
   174	wire your `DataActorCore` field into the runtime contract. Your type
   175	implements or derives `Debug`; the macro supplies the native runtime wiring.
   176	User code normally uses the `DataActor` facade methods for subscriptions,
   177	cache access, and clock access.
   178	
   179	### Handler methods
   180	
   181	Override any handler on the `DataActor` trait to receive the corresponding
   182	data or event. All handlers have default no-op implementations, so you only
   183	override what you need.
   184	
   185	| Handler                | Receives                  |
   186	| ---------------------- | ------------------------- |
   187	| `on_start`             | Actor started.            |
   188	| `on_stop`              | Actor stopped.            |
   189	| `on_quote`             | `QuoteTick`               |
   190	| `on_trade`             | `TradeTick`               |
   191	| `on_bar`               | `Bar`                     |
   192	| `on_book_deltas`       | `OrderBookDeltas`         |
   193	| `on_book`              | `OrderBook` (at interval) |
   194	| `on_instrument`        | `InstrumentAny`           |
   195	| `on_mark_price`        | `MarkPriceUpdate`         |
   196	| `on_index_price`       | `IndexPriceUpdate`        |
   197	| `on_funding_rate`      | `FundingRateUpdate`       |
   198	| `on_option_greeks`     | `OptionGreeks`            |
   199	| `on_option_chain`      | `OptionChainSlice`        |
   200	| `on_instrument_status` | `InstrumentStatus`        |
   201	| `on_time_event`        | `TimeEvent`               |
   202	
   203	For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the
   204	[Write an Actor (Rust)](../how_to/write_rust_actor.md) how-to guide.
   205	For a complete example, see
   206	[`BookImbalanceActor`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/trading/src/examples/actors/imbalance).
   207	
   208	## Strategies
   209	
   210	A strategy extends an actor with order management. Implement `DataActor` for
   211	data handling and use `nautilus_strategy!` to wire your `StrategyCore` field
   212	into the strategy runtime contract. `StrategyCore` stores the runtime strategy
   213	state; normal strategy logic reaches it through facade methods on `self`.
   214	Runtime registration requires the native wiring generated by the macro, but
   215	normal strategy logic uses `Strategy` methods and the facade methods on `self`.
   216	Strategies also override order event handlers on the `Strategy` trait, such as
   217	`on_order_filled` (`OrderFilled`) and `on_order_canceled` (`OrderCanceled`).
   218	
   219	### Order management
   220	
   221	The `Strategy` trait provides order methods through the facade:
   222	
   223	| Method                | Action                                    |
   224	| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
   225	| `submit_order`        | Submit a new order to the venue.          |
   226	| `submit_order_list`   | Submit a list of contingent orders.       |
   227	| `modify_order`        | Modify price, quantity, or trigger price. |
   228	| `cancel_order`        | Cancel a specific order.                  |
   229	| `cancel_orders`       | Cancel a filtered set of orders.          |
   230	| `cancel_all_orders`   | Cancel all orders for an instrument.      |
   231	| `close_position`      | Close a position with a market order.     |
   232	| `close_all_positions` | Close all open positions.                 |
   233	
   234	The `OrderApi` (accessed via `self.order()`) builds orders and order lists:
   235	
   236	- `generate_client_order_id`
   237	- `generate_order_list_id`
   238	- `market`
   239	- `limit`
   240	- `stop_market`
   241	- `stop_limit`
   242	- `market_to_limit`
   243	- `market_if_touched`
   244	- `limit_if_touched`
   245	- `trailing_stop_market`
   246	- `trailing_stop_limit`
   247	- `bracket`
   248	- `create_list`
   249	
   250	### Core wiring macros
   251	
   252	Rust actors, strategies, and execution algorithms keep their runtime core as a
   253	struct field. The macros tell the traits where that field lives.
   254	
   255	| Macro                                          | Core field               | Generates                      |
   256	| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
   257	| `nautilus_actor!(Type)`                        | `DataActorCore`          | Runtime wiring.                |
   258	| `nautilus_strategy!(Type)`                     | `StrategyCore`           | Runtime wiring and `Strategy`. |
   259	| `nautilus_execution_algorithm!(Type, { ... })` | `ExecutionAlgorithmCore` | Runtime wiring and algorithm.  |
   260	
   261	The macros expect a field named `core`; pass a field name as the second
   262	argument when needed. They do not make the actor, strategy, or `StrategyCore`
   263	deref to runtime internals.
   264	The execution algorithm macro takes an `on_order()` implementation block because
   265	that method defines the algorithm's required order handling.
   266	
   267	### Native traits
   268	
   269	Use facade methods by default:
   270	
   271	- `actor_id()`
   272	- `trader_id()`
   273	- `is_registered()`
   274	- `config()`
   275	- `strategy_id()`
   276	- `clock()`
   277	- `cache()`
   278	- `order()`
   279	- `portfolio()`
   280	
   281	`DataActorNative`, `StrategyNative`, and `ExecutionAlgorithmNative` are for
   282	native-only access below that facade. This section documents engine, runtime, and explicit
   283	latency-sensitive native Rust code, not the portable authoring path.
   284	
   285	| Authoring path            | Native traits?   | Normal API                          |
   286	| ------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------- |
   287	| Native Rust binary        | Only when needed | `Strategy` and `DataActor` facades. |
   288	| Rust launched from Python | Only when needed | Same as native Rust.                |
   289	| Python-authored component | No               | Facades only.                       |
   290	
   291	Native traits expose borrowed core state, `Rc<RefCell<_>>`, and runtime
   292	references. Use them when native Rust code intentionally accepts those borrow
   293	rules for an explicit latency-sensitive path. Engine, runtime, registration,
   294	PyO3, and testkit code can import `DataActorNative`, `StrategyNative`, or
   295	`ExecutionAlgorithmNative` when they need actor-core, strategy-core, or
   296	execution-algorithm-core access. Do not use them in ordinary portable actor,
   297	strategy, or execution algorithm logic or Python-authored components, because
   298	those types do not cross the Python boundary.
   299	
   300	`ExecutionAlgorithmCore` owns a `DataActorCore`, but it does not deref to one.
   301	Normal execution algorithm logic should use `id()`, `actor_id()`,
   302	`trader_id()`, `clock()`, and `cache()`. Reach for `ExecutionAlgorithmNative`
   303	only when the code needs native execution-algorithm state.
   304	
   305	Choose the smallest native handle and keep each borrow scoped. Use `order()`
   306	for normal strategy order construction. Reach for
   307	`order_factory()` only when native code needs the raw mutable factory borrow.
   308	
   309	#### `DataActorNative` methods
   310	
   311	| Native method | Return shape             | Use when                        |
   312	| ------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
   313	| `core()`      | `&DataActorCore`         | Read actor internals.           |
   314	| `core_mut()`  | `&mut DataActorCore`     | Mutate actor internals.         |
   315	| `clock_mut()` | `RefMut<'_, dyn Clock>`  | Need a mutable clock borrow.    |
   316	| `clock_rc()`  | `Rc<RefCell<dyn Clock>>` | Store or pass the shared clock. |
   317	| `cache_ref()` | `Ref<'_, Cache>`         | Need short live-cache reads.    |
   318	| `cache_rc()`  | `Rc<RefCell<Cache>>`     | Mutate, store, or pass cache.   |
   319	
   320	#### `StrategyNative` methods
   321	
   322	| Native method         | Return shape                | Use when                         |
   323	| --------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
   324	| `strategy_core()`     | `&StrategyCore`             | Read strategy internals.         |
   325	| `strategy_core_mut()` | `&mut StrategyCore`         | Mutate strategy internals.       |
   326	| `order_factory()`     | `RefMut<'_, OrderFactory>`  | Need raw mutable factory borrow. |
   327	| `order_factory_rc()`  | `Rc<RefCell<OrderFactory>>` | Store or pass the factory.       |
   328	| `portfolio_rc()`      | `Rc<RefCell<Portfolio>>`    | Store or pass the portfolio.     |
   329	
   330	#### `ExecutionAlgorithmNative` methods
   331	
   332	| Native method               | Return shape                  | Use when                              |
   333	| --------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
   334	| `exec_algorithm_core()`     | `&ExecutionAlgorithmCore`     | Read execution algorithm internals.   |
   335	| `exec_algorithm_core_mut()` | `&mut ExecutionAlgorithmCore` | Mutate execution algorithm internals. |
   336	
   337	For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the
   338	[Write a Strategy (Rust)](../how_to/write_rust_strategy.md) how-to guide.
   339	For complete examples, see
   340	[`EmaCross`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/trading/src/examples/strategies/ema_cross)
   341	and
   342	[`GridMarketMaker`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/trading/src/examples/strategies/grid_mm).
   343	
   344	### Running Rust components
   345	
   346	Rust strategies and actors can run through two paths. The examples
   347	below use strategies, but the same pattern applies to bundled actors via
   348	`add_actor` (pure Rust) and `add_builtin_actor` (from Python).
   349	
   350	#### Pure Rust
   351	
   352	Write your strategy and `main` function in Rust, then build a standalone
   353	binary with `cargo build`. This path requires no Python runtime.
   354	
   355	```rust
   356	let strategy = GridMarketMaker::new(config);
   357	node.add_strategy(strategy)?;
   358	node.run().await?;
   359	```
   360	
   361	See [Run Live Trading (Rust)](../how_to/run_rust_live_trading.md) for a
   362	full walkthrough.
   363	
   364	#### Built-in examples from Python
   365	
   366	Pass a type name and config to `add_builtin_strategy` to register a
   367	built-in example strategy from Python. This path exists to single-source
   368	the bundled example strategy code across Rust and Python docs, examples,
   369	and tests. It is not a first-class extension path for adding native
   370	strategies. For custom native components, use pure Rust.
   371	
   372	```python
   373	from nautilus_trader.trading import GridMarketMakerConfig
   374	
   375	config = GridMarketMakerConfig(
   376	    instrument_id=InstrumentId.from_str("BTC-USDT-SWAP.OKX"),
   377	    max_position=Quantity.from_str("10.0"),
   378	    trade_size=Quantity.from_str("0.1"),
   379	    num_levels=5,
   380	    grid_step_bps=15,
   381	)
   382	
   383	node.add_builtin_strategy("GridMarketMaker", config)
   384	```
   385	
   386	Built-in strategy configs:
   387	
   388	| Config                       | Strategy               |
   389	| ---------------------------- | ---------------------- |
   390	| `CompositeMarketMakerConfig` | `CompositeMarketMaker` |
   391	| `DeltaNeutralVolConfig`      | `DeltaNeutralVol`      |
   392	| `EmaCrossConfig`             | `EmaCross`             |
   393	| `ExecTesterConfig`           | `ExecTester`           |
   394	| `GridMarketMakerConfig`      | `GridMarketMaker`      |
   395	| `HurstVpinDirectionalConfig` | `HurstVpinDirectional` |
   396	
   397	`add_builtin_actor` follows the same bundled-only rule for actors used by
   398	examples and tests.
   399	
   400	Built-in actor configs (via `add_builtin_actor`):
   401	
   402	| Config                     | Actor                |
   403	| -------------------------- | -------------------- |
   404	| `BookImbalanceActorConfig` | `BookImbalanceActor` |
   405	| `DataTesterConfig`         | `DataTester`         |

   407	## Backtesting
   408	
   409	For annotated walkthroughs of both APIs, see the
   410	[Run a Backtest (Rust)](../how_to/run_rust_backtest.md) how-to guide.
   411	
   412	### `BacktestEngine` (low-level API)
   413	
   414	Construct the engine, add venues and instruments, load data, register
   415	strategies, and run. See the full working example:
   416	
   417	```bash
   418	cargo run -p nautilus-backtest --features examples --example engine-ema-cross
   419	```
   420	
   421	Source:
   422	[`crates/backtest/examples/engine_ema_cross.rs`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/backtest/examples/engine_ema_cross.rs)
   423	
   424	### `BacktestNode` (high-level API)
   425	
   426	Loads data from a `ParquetDataCatalog` and supports streaming in
   427	configurable chunk sizes. Requires the `streaming` feature on
   428	`nautilus-backtest`. See the full working example:
   429	
   430	```bash
   431	cargo run -p nautilus-backtest --features examples,streaming --example node-ema-cross
   432	```
   433	
   434	Source:
   435	[`crates/backtest/examples/node_ema_cross.rs`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/backtest/examples/node_ema_cross.rs)
   436

   453	| Bybit               | `crates/adapters/bybit/examples/`               |

     1	# Write a Strategy (Rust)
     2	
     3	A strategy extends an actor with order management. This guide walks through
     4	building a minimal strategy that subscribes to quotes and submits market
     5	orders. Read [Write an Actor (Rust)](write_rust_actor.md) first.
     6	
     7	For background on strategy concepts and order management, see the
     8	[Strategies](../concepts/strategies.md) and [Rust](../concepts/rust.md)
     9	concept guides.
    10	
    11	## Define the struct
    12	
    13	A strategy stores a `StrategyCore` field for runtime wiring. Normal strategy
    14	logic does not use the field directly; use the facade methods on `self`.
    15	
    16	```rust
    17	use nautilus_common::actor::DataActor;
    18	use nautilus_model::{
    19	    data::QuoteTick,
    20	    enums::OrderSide,
    21	    identifiers::{InstrumentId, StrategyId},
    22	    types::Quantity,
    23	};
    24	use nautilus_trading::{nautilus_strategy, strategy::{Strategy, StrategyConfig, StrategyCore}};
    25	
    26	pub struct MyStrategy {
    27	    core: StrategyCore,
    28	    instrument_id: InstrumentId,
    29	    trade_size: Quantity,
    30	}
    31	```
    32	
    33	## Implement the constructor
    34	
    35	`StrategyConfig` takes a `strategy_id` and an `order_id_tag`. The tag is
    36	appended to all client order IDs from this strategy, preventing collisions
    37	when multiple strategies trade the same instrument.
    38	
    39	The tag cannot contain a hyphen, because the runtime reads it back from the
    40	final hyphen-separated part of the strategy ID. `StrategyCore::new` panics on
    41	an invalid tag; use `StrategyCore::new_checked` to handle it as an error
    42	instead.
    43	
    44	```rust
    45	impl MyStrategy {
    46	    pub fn new(instrument_id: InstrumentId) -> Self {
    47	        let config = StrategyConfig {
    48	            strategy_id: Some(StrategyId::from("MY_STRAT-001")),
    49	            order_id_tag: Some("001".to_string()),
    50	            ..Default::default()
    51	        };
    52	        Self {
    53	            core: StrategyCore::new(config),
    54	            instrument_id,
    55	            trade_size: Quantity::from("1.0"),
    56	        }
    57	    }
    58	}
    59	```
    60	
    61	## Wire up the core and implement Debug
    62	
    63	The `nautilus_strategy!` macro generates the native runtime wiring used by
    64	registration and the `Strategy` trait impl. By default it delegates to a field
    65	named `core`; pass a second argument for a different field name. The macro
    66	does not make your strategy or its `StrategyCore` deref to runtime internals.
    67	It also adds `config()`, which returns the `StrategyConfig` passed to
    68	`StrategyCore::new`.
    69	
    70	Runtime registration uses blanket `Actor` and `Component` implementations that
    71	require native wiring and `Debug`. The macro supplies the native wiring;
    72	implement `Debug` manually or derive it.
    73	
    74	```rust
    75	nautilus_strategy!(MyStrategy);
    76	
    77	impl std::fmt::Debug for MyStrategy {
    78	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
    79	        f.debug_struct("MyStrategy").finish()
    80	    }
    81	}
    82	```
    83	
    84	## Implement the DataActor trait
    85	
    86	Data handling works the same as in an actor. Subscribe in `on_start`,
    87	respond in handlers.
    88	
    89	```rust
    90	impl DataActor for MyStrategy {
    91	    fn on_start(&mut self) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    92	        self.subscribe_quotes(self.instrument_id, None, None);
    93	        Ok(())
    94	    }
    95	
    96	    fn on_quote(&mut self, quote: &QuoteTick) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    97	        let order = self.order().market(
    98	            self.instrument_id,
    99	            OrderSide::Buy,
   100	            self.trade_size,
   101	            None, None, None, None, None, None, None,
   102	        );
   103	        self.submit_order(order, None, None, None)?;
   104	        Ok(())
   105	    }
   106	}
   107	```
   108	
   109	`self.order()` builds orders and order lists. Available methods:
   110	
   111	- `market`
   112	- `limit`
   113	- `stop_market`
   114	- `stop_limit`
   115	- `market_to_limit`
   116	- `market_if_touched`
   117	- `limit_if_touched`
   118	- `trailing_stop_market`
   119	- `trailing_stop_limit`
   120	- `bracket`
   121	- `create_list`
   122	- `generate_client_order_id`
   123	- `generate_order_list_id`
   124	
   125	`submit_order` is available on `self` through the `Strategy` trait impl
   126	generated by the macro.
   127	
   128	## Native runtime access
   129	
   130	Use the public facade in strategy logic:
   131	
   132	- `clock()`
   133	- `cache()`
   134	- `order()`
   135	- `portfolio()`
   136	- `strategy_id()`
   137	- The order management methods on `Strategy`
   138	
   139	Normal strategy code does not import `DataActorNative` or `StrategyNative`, and
   140	does not call native handles such as:
   141	
   142	- `core()`
   143	- `core_mut()`
   144	- `strategy_core()`
   145	- `strategy_core_mut()`
   146	- `order_factory()`
   147	- `order_factory_rc()`
   148	- `portfolio_rc()`
   149	
   150	Those native handles expose borrowed runtime state and stay in engine, runtime,
   151	registration, PyO3, testkit, or explicit latency-sensitive native code. The [Rust native traits](../concepts/rust.md#native-traits) section
   152	covers the native-traits applicability matrix and these method tables:
   153	
   154	- [`DataActorNative` methods](../concepts/rust.md#dataactornative-methods)
   155	- [`StrategyNative` methods](../concepts/rust.md#strategynative-methods)
   156	
   157	## Override Strategy hooks
   158	
   159	To override `Strategy` trait methods such as order or position event
   160	handlers, pass them in a block. The macro generates the internal plumbing
   161	automatically; keep `DataActor` handlers in the separate `impl DataActor`
   162	block.
   163	
   164	```rust
   165	nautilus_strategy!(MyStrategy, {
   166	    fn on_order_rejected(&mut self, event: OrderRejected) {
   167	        log::warn!("Order rejected: {}", event.reason);
   168	    }
   169	});
   170	```
   171	
   172	## Order management methods
   173	
   174	The `Strategy` trait provides these facade methods:
   175	
   176	| Method                | Action                                          |
   177	| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
   178	| `submit_order`        | Submit a new order to the venue.                |
   179	| `submit_order_list`   | Submit a list of contingent orders.             |
   180	| `modify_order`        | Modify price, quantity, or trigger price.       |
   181	| `modify_orders`       | Modify multiple orders for the same instrument. |
   182	| `cancel_order`        | Cancel a specific order.                        |
   183	| `cancel_orders`       | Cancel a filtered set of orders.                |
   184	| `cancel_all_orders`   | Cancel all orders for an instrument.            |
   185	| `close_position`      | Close a position with a market order.           |
   186	| `close_all_positions` | Close all open positions.                       |
   187	
   188	## Full examples
   189	
   190	- [`EmaCross`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/trading/src/examples/strategies/ema_cross):
   191	  Dual-EMA crossover with indicator integration.
   192	- [`GridMarketMaker`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/trading/src/examples/strategies/grid_mm):
   193	  Grid market making with configurable levels and requoting.

# %% [markdown]
# # Backtest with FX Bar Data
#
# Run an EMA cross strategy on USD/JPY 1-minute bid/ask bars with FX rollover
# interest and a probabilistic fill model. The data ships with the
# NautilusTrader test kit, so this tutorial runs without any external download.
#
# [View source on GitHub](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/blob/develop/docs/tutorials/backtest_fx_bars.py).

# %% [markdown]
# ## Introduction
#
# The strategy is `EMACross`, a teaching example that compares a fast EMA
# against a slow EMA on bar closes:
#
# - **Fast EMA crosses above slow EMA**: any short position is closed and a new
#   long is opened.
# - **Fast EMA crosses below slow EMA**: any long position is closed and a new
#   short is opened.
#
# The venue is a simulated FX ECN with a `MARGIN` account, `HEDGING` OMS, and
# multi-currency starting balances of 1,000,000 USD and 10,000,000 JPY. A
# `FillModel` introduces a 50% probability of one-tick slippage, and the
# `FXRolloverInterestModule` applies daily rollover at the relevant short-term
# interest differential.
#
# `EMACross` is a teaching strategy and has no edge.
#
# ```mermaid
# flowchart LR
#     subgraph Inputs ["Data streams"]
#         B["1-minute BID bar (FXCM)"]
#         A["1-minute ASK bar (FXCM)"]
#     end
#
#     subgraph Wrangler ["QuoteTickDataWrangler"]
#         Q["QuoteTick stream"]
#     end
#
#     subgraph Engine ["Backtest engine"]
#         AGG["5-minute BID INTERNAL aggregator"]
#         BAR["Bar close"]
#         F1(("EMA(10)"))
#         F2(("EMA(20)"))
#     end
#
#     subgraph Decision ["Crossover decision"]
#         X{{"fast >= slow"}}
#         Y{{"fast < slow"}}
#     end
#
#     subgraph Orders ["Orders"]
#         L["Close shorts -> BUY market"]
#         S["Close longs  -> SELL market"]
#     end
#
#     B --> Q
#     A --> Q
#     Q --> AGG --> BAR
#     BAR --> F1 --> X
#     BAR --> F2 --> X
#     F1 --> Y
#     F2 --> Y
#     X -->|cross up| L
#     Y -->|cross down| S
# ```

# %% [markdown]
# ## Prerequisites
#
# - Python 3.12+
# - [NautilusTrader](https://pypi.org/project/nautilus_trader/) 2.x installed
#   (`pip install -U --pre nautilus_trader`). The `visualization` extra is only
#   needed if you also want to regenerate the panels at the end of the tutorial.
# - pandas (`pip install pandas`). The wheel declares no runtime dependencies.
# - The sibling [`ema_cross.py`](./ema_cross.py) file. Keep it next to this
#   tutorial when downloading or converting it with Jupytext.

# %%
from decimal import Decimal

from nautilus_trader.common import LogLevel
from nautilus_trader.config import BacktestEngineConfig
from nautilus_trader.backtest import BacktestEngine
from nautilus_trader.backtest import FXRolloverInterestModule
from nautilus_trader.backtest import InterestRateRecord
from nautilus_trader.config import LoggerConfig
from nautilus_trader.config import RiskEngineConfig
from nautilus_trader.execution import ProbabilisticFillModel
from nautilus_trader.model import AccountType
from nautilus_trader.model import BarType
from nautilus_trader.model import Currency
from nautilus_trader.model import Money
from nautilus_trader.model import OmsType
from nautilus_trader.model import TraderId
from nautilus_trader.model import Venue
from nautilus_trader.testkit.providers import TestDataProvider
from nautilus_trader.testkit.providers import TestInstrumentProvider

from ema_cross import EMACross
from ema_cross import EMACrossConfig


JPY = Currency.from_str("JPY")
USD = Currency.from_str("USD")


# %% [markdown]
# ## Engine setup
#
# Pre-trade risk checks are bypassed so the strategy's market orders flow
# straight through to the matching engine.

# %%
config = BacktestEngineConfig(
    trader_id=TraderId.from_str("BACKTESTER-001"),
    logging=LoggerConfig(stdout_level=LogLevel.ERROR),
    risk_engine=RiskEngineConfig(bypass=True),
)
engine = BacktestEngine(config=config)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Simulation modules
#
# `FXRolloverInterestModule` charges or credits rollover interest on open
# positions at the configured cutover time, using the bundled
# `short-term-interest.csv` rates from the OECD short-term interest series.
# Without it a backtest spanning many sessions ignores carry.

# %%
provider = TestDataProvider()
interest_rate_data = provider.read_csv("short-term-interest.csv")
interest_rate_records = [
    InterestRateRecord(location=row.LOCATION, time=row.TIME, value=row.Value)
    for row in interest_rate_data.itertuples(index=False)
]
fx_rollover_interest = FXRolloverInterestModule(records=interest_rate_records)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Fill model
#
# Limit orders fill on a 20% probability per tick when their price is reached,
# and any market or marketable order draws a one-tick slip on a 50% coin flip.
# The seed makes the run reproducible.

# %%
fill_model = ProbabilisticFillModel(
    prob_fill_on_limit=0.2,
    prob_slippage=0.5,
    random_seed=42,
)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Venue
#
# `OmsType.HEDGING` lets the strategy carry concurrent long and short positions
# in the same instrument and have the venue assign position IDs. The account is
# multi-currency so PnL on USD/JPY accrues in JPY rather than being converted
# on every fill.

# %%
SIM = Venue("SIM")
engine.add_venue(
    venue=SIM,
    oms_type=OmsType.HEDGING,
    account_type=AccountType.MARGIN,
    base_currency=None,
    starting_balances=[Money(1_000_000, USD), Money(10_000_000, JPY)],
    fill_model=fill_model,
    modules=[fx_rollover_interest],
)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Instrument and data
#
# `TestDataProvider.quotes_from_fxcm_bars` synthesizes quote ticks from each
# minute's open, high, low, and close in the bundled FXCM bid and ask CSVs.
# The strategy declares `5-MINUTE-BID-INTERNAL`, so the engine builds 5-minute
# BID bars from the quote stream internally.

# %%
USDJPY_SIM = TestInstrumentProvider.default_fx_ccy("USD/JPY", SIM)
engine.add_instrument(USDJPY_SIM)

ticks = provider.quotes_from_fxcm_bars(
    instrument=USDJPY_SIM,
    bid_csv="fxcm/usdjpy-m1-bid-2013.csv",
    ask_csv="fxcm/usdjpy-m1-ask-2013.csv",
)
engine.add_data(ticks)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Strategy
#
# Trade size is one million USD per order. EMACross cancels and replaces the
# position on every crossover, so the strategy is in some position for nearly
# the whole month.

# %%
strategy_config = EMACrossConfig(
    instrument_id=USDJPY_SIM.id,
    bar_type=BarType.from_str("USD/JPY.SIM-5-MINUTE-BID-INTERNAL"),
    fast_ema_period=10,
    slow_ema_period=20,
    trade_size=Decimal(1_000_000),
)
strategy = EMACross(config=strategy_config)
engine.add_strategy(strategy=strategy)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Run
#
# The engine processes every quote tick and bar in timestamp order, then
# returns when the data is exhausted.

# %%
engine.run()

# %% [markdown]
# ## Reports
#
# `engine.generate_*` returns DataFrames covering the account state, the
# fills, and the closed positions.

# %%
engine.generate_account_report(SIM)

# %%
engine.generate_order_fills_report()

# %%
engine.generate_positions_report()

# %% [markdown]
# ## What the run produces
#
# A 28-day run prints 8,065 5-minute bars and triggers 234 closed cycles
# across 468 fills (every crossover after the first emits a closing fill on
# the previous position and an opening fill on the new one). 72 of the 234
# cycles are profitable. The strategy ends down 209,000 JPY: a textbook
# whipsaw signature on a noisy 5-minute series.
#
# ![USD/JPY 5-minute close with EMAs across the month](./assets/backtest_fx_bars/panel_a_price_overview.png)
#
# **Figure 1.** *USD/JPY BID close at 5-minute resolution across 2013-02 with
# EMA(10) and EMA(20) overlaid. Long flat patches are weekend gaps in the FXCM
# bid feed.*
#
# ![Three-day zoom on crossovers](./assets/backtest_fx_bars/panel_b_zoom.png)
