 `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-zhouhanru-Documents-David-Program-agent-skills/50601428-44f8-470f-84e7-e94a5878b418/scratchpad/nt-eval/iteration-1/eval-migrate-v1-to-v2/without_skill/outputs/work/MIGRATION_V2.md`

````text
1	# Migrate from v1 to v2
2	
3	NautilusTrader v2 is the Rust core and PyO3 Python package under `python/`. It is the primary Python
4	path on `develop`. Use this guide to migrate from the legacy v1 Cython package.
5	
6	Legacy v1 lives on the `develop_v1` branch, which accepts critical security backports for
7	approximately three months after the v2 cutover. It does not receive new feature or parity work.
8	
9	The v1 and v2 packages both install and import as `nautilus_trader`, so use a separate virtual
10	environment for each and never install both into one.
11	
12	## Install v2
13	
14	Install a release candidate from PyPI in a fresh environment:
15	
16	```bash
17	uv venv --python 3.14
18	source .venv/bin/activate
19	uv pip install --pre nautilus_trader
20	```
21	
22	Run this block outside a NautilusTrader source checkout. The repository's `exclude-newer` uv policy
23	can filter out newly published release-candidate wheels.
24	
25	To build from source, build the package from the repository root:
26	
27	```bash
28	make build-debug
29	uv run --project python --no-sync python -c \
30	  'import nautilus_trader; print(nautilus_trader.__version__)'
31	```
32	
33	The source build uses the `python/.venv` and `target/` directories.
34	See [Installation](docs/getting_started/installation.md) for platform support and package-index options.
35	
36	## Port Python code
37	
38	Core strategy, data, order, risk, portfolio, backtest, and live workflows remain available. Update
39	imports and configuration to the new module paths:
40	
41	| v1 path                                                        | v2 path                                                   |
42	| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
43	| `nautilus_trader.backtest.engine.BacktestEngine`               | `nautilus_trader.backtest.BacktestEngine`                 |
44	| `nautilus_trader.backtest.node.BacktestNode`                   | `nautilus_trader.backtest.BacktestNode`                   |
45	| `nautilus_trader.live.node.TradingNode`                        | `nautilus_trader.live.LiveNode`                           |
46	| `nautilus_trader.model.enums.OrderSide`                        | `nautilus_trader.model.OrderSide`                         |
47	| `nautilus_trader.model.identifiers.TraderId`                   | `nautilus_trader.model.TraderId`                          |
48	| `nautilus_trader.config.StrategyConfig`                        | `nautilus_trader.config.StrategyConfig`                   |
49	| Adapter classes from `nautilus_trader.adapters.<venue>.config` | Rust/PyO3 classes from `nautilus_trader.adapters.<venue>` |
50	
51	### Common API renames
52	
53	V2 shortens common strategy and cache names. The `QuoteTick`, `TradeTick`, and
54	`register_indicator_for_*_ticks` names do not change.
55	
56	| v1 name                              | v2 name                        |
57	| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
58	| `on_quote_tick`                      | `on_quote`                     |
59	| `on_trade_tick`                      | `on_trade`                     |
60	| `on_order_book`                      | `on_book`                      |
61	| `on_order_book_deltas`               | `on_book_deltas`               |
62	| `on_order_book_depth`                | `on_book_depth`                |
63	| `subscribe_quote_ticks`              | `subscribe_quotes`             |
64	| `subscribe_trade_ticks`              | `subscribe_trades`             |
65	| `unsubscribe_quote_ticks`            | `unsubscribe_quotes`           |
66	| `unsubscribe_trade_ticks`            | `unsubscribe_trades`           |
67	| `request_quote_ticks`                | `request_quotes`               |
68	| `request_trade_ticks`                | `request_trades`               |
69	| `subscribe_order_book_deltas`        | `subscribe_book_deltas`        |
70	| `subscribe_order_book_depth`         | `subscribe_book_depth10`       |
71	| `subscribe_order_book_at_interval`   | `subscribe_book_at_interval`   |
72	| `unsubscribe_order_book_deltas`      | `unsubscribe_book_deltas`      |
73	| `unsubscribe_order_book_depth`       | `unsubscribe_book_depth10`     |
74	| `unsubscribe_order_book_at_interval` | `unsubscribe_book_at_interval` |
75	| `request_order_book_snapshot`        | `request_book_snapshot`        |
76	| `request_order_book_deltas`          | `request_book_deltas`          |
77	| `request_order_book_depth`           | `request_book_depth`           |
78	| `cache.quote_tick`                   | `cache.quote`                  |
79	| `cache.trade_tick`                   | `cache.trade`                  |
80	| `cache.quote_ticks`                  | `cache.quotes`                 |
81	| `cache.trade_ticks`                  | `cache.trades`                 |
82	| `cache.quote_tick_count`             | `cache.quote_count`            |
83	| `cache.trade_tick_count`             | `cache.trade_count`            |
84	
85	### API changes
86	
87	V2 uses specific names for component and model identities:
88	
89	| v1 member          | v2 member                              |
90	| ------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
91	| `Actor.id`         | `DataActor.actor_id`                   |
92	| `Strategy.id`      | `Strategy.strategy_id`                 |
93	| `ExecAlgorithm.id` | `ExecutionAlgorithm.exec_algorithm_id` |
94	| Event `id`         | `event_id`                             |
95	| Report `id`        | `report_id`                            |
96	| Account `type`     | `account_type`                         |
97	
98	Collection and lifecycle inspection also changes shape:
99	
100	| v1 member                      | v2 member                                                    |
101	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
102	| `Order.events`                 | `Order.events()`                                             |
103	| `Position.adjustments`         | `Position.adjustments()`                                     |
104	| `Position.client_order_ids`    | `Position.client_order_ids()`                                |
105	| `Position.events`              | `Position.events()`                                          |
106	| `Position.trade_ids`           | `Position.trade_ids()`                                       |
107	| `Position.venue_order_ids`     | `Position.venue_order_ids()`                                 |
108	| `OrderList.orders`             | `client_order_ids()`, then resolve each ID through the cache |
109	| `OrderList.first`              | Resolve `first_client_order_id` through the cache            |
110	| `Portfolio.initialized`        | `Portfolio.is_initialized()`                                 |
111	| `Portfolio.analyzer`           | `statistics()`, `snapshots()`, and `register_statistic()`    |
112	| `Actor.state`/`Strategy.state` | `DataActor.state()`/`Strategy.state()`                       |
113	| `ExecAlgorithm.state`          | `ExecutionAlgorithm.state` remains a property                |
114	| `Component.is_running`         | `is_running()`                                               |
115	| `Component.is_stopped`         | `is_stopped()`                                               |
116	| `Component.is_disposed`        | `is_disposed()`                                              |
117	| `Component.is_degraded`        | `is_degraded()`                                              |
118	| `Component.is_faulted`         | `is_faulted()`                                               |
119	
120	Portfolio query names also change without compatibility aliases:
121	
122	| v1 name                | v2 name                            |
123	| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
124	| `margins_init()`       | `instrument_initial_margins()`     |
125	| `margins_maint()`      | `instrument_maintenance_margins()` |
126	| `is_flat()`            | `is_net_flat()`                    |
127	| `is_completely_flat()` | `is_completely_net_flat()`         |
128	
129	`unrealized_pnl()`, `total_pnl()`, and `net_exposure()` implement the retained optional `price`
130	parameter as a fresh calculation that does not replace cached values. `realized_pnl()`,
131	`realized_pnls()`, `unrealized_pnl()`, `unrealized_pnls()`, `total_pnl()`, `total_pnls()`,
132	`net_exposure()`, and `net_exposures()` accept `target_currency` and fail closed when a required
133	price or conversion is unavailable or exact arithmetic overflows. Collection queries never return
134	partial results. When a query accepts both `venue` and `account_id`, those scopes must identify the
135	same account.
136	
137	`account()` returns a detached account value. `build_snapshot()` returns an on-demand
138	sample without recording it, and the Python Portfolio does not expose engine mutation commands or
139	the internal recorded realized-PnL cache.
140	
141	V1 `is_initialized` means that a component has advanced beyond `PRE_INITIALIZED`. V2 `is_ready()`
142	means exactly `READY`, so it is not an equivalent replacement while a component is running,
143	stopped, degraded, disposed, or faulted. Inspect `state()` on `DataActor` and `Strategy`, or the
144	`state` property on `ExecutionAlgorithm`, and compare it with `ComponentState.PRE_INITIALIZED`.
145	
146	Read the v1 `Strategy` runtime properties `order_id_tag`, `oms_type`, `manage_contingent_orders`,
147	`manage_gtd_expiry`, `use_uuid_client_order_ids`, and `use_hyphens_in_client_order_ids` through the
148	same-name properties on `Strategy.config`. Read the configured v1 `external_order_claims` value
149	through `Strategy.config.external_order_instrument_ids`. In v2, that field records serializable
150	configuration intent; call `Strategy.set_external_order_instrument_ids(...)` after registration to
151	replace the active claims. The two client-order-ID formatting options on a strategy-owned
152	`OrderFactory` use the same config. A standalone factory has no equivalent flag readback.
153	
154	Historical requests use type-specific batch callbacks in v2:
155	
156	| v1 data through `on_historical_data` | v2 callback                   | v2 argument                                |
157	| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
158	| Custom data                          | `on_historical_data`          | One `CustomData` or `Sequence[CustomData]` |
159	| Book snapshot                        | `on_book`                     | One `OrderBook`                            |
160	| Book deltas                          | `on_historical_book_deltas`   | `Sequence[OrderBookDelta]`                 |
161	| Book depth                           | `on_historical_book_depth`    | `Sequence[OrderBookDepth10]`               |
162	| Quote ticks                          | `on_historical_quotes`        | `Sequence[QuoteTick]`                      |
163	| Trade ticks                          | `on_historical_trades`        | `Sequence[TradeTick]`                      |
164	| Funding rates                        | `on_historical_funding_rates` | `Sequence[FundingRateUpdate]`              |
165	| Bars                                 | `on_historical_bars`          | `Sequence[Bar]`                            |
166	
167	Typed historical results no longer fall through to `on_historical_data`; that hook handles custom
168	data. A response carrying one `CustomData` arrives as that object; a response carrying a batch
169	arrives as one list, including an empty list. `on_historical_mark_prices` and
170	`on_historical_index_prices` are available for native batch delivery, but the current public Python
171	API does not initiate those requests.
172	
173	The generic `on_event` hook is removed. Replace timer handling with `on_time_event`, aggregate order
174	handling with `on_order_event`, and aggregate position handling with `on_position_event`. For
175	custom messaging, use `on_signal` or a typed data subscription instead of overriding `on_event`.
176	
177	Python v2 `ExecutionAlgorithm` does not inherit the full actor surface. Move market-data and
178	historical callbacks to `DataActor` or `Strategy`. Its inherited v1 `on_save` and `on_load` hooks
179	also have no v2 algorithm callback; retain that state in application configuration or move the
180	stateful component to `DataActor` or `Strategy`. Change `on_order_list(self, order_list)` to
181	`on_order_list(self, order_list, orders)`.
182	
183	V2 strategy order changes take client order IDs rather than order objects:
184	
185	| v1 method                    | v2 method                                  |
186	| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
187	| `modify_order(order, ...)`   | `modify_order(order.client_order_id, ...)` |
188	| `cancel_order(order, ...)`   | `cancel_order(order.client_order_id, ...)` |
189	| `cancel_orders(orders, ...)` | `cancel_orders(client_order_ids, ...)`     |
190	
191	`Strategy.cancel_all_orders()` now affects only orders associated with that strategy by default.
192	Pass `strategy_only=False` to retain v1's broader instrument-and-side scope.
193	
194	The public `nautilus_trader.data.OptionChainManager` is removed. Call `subscribe_option_chain(...)`
195	from a `DataActor` or `Strategy`, then handle each aggregated `OptionChainSlice` in
196	`on_option_chain(slice)`. Call `unsubscribe_option_chain(series_id)` to stop the subscription.
197	
198	`Cache.actor_ids()` is removed. Rust integrations can use `Trader::actor_ids()`; Python v2 does not
199	expose a direct actor-ID collection.
200	
201	### Typed model objects
202	
203	V2 removes the PyCapsule boundary between Python and Rust. Pass model objects directly and use
204	normal Python type checks:
205	
206	| v1 API                                        | v2 migration                                  |
207	| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
208	| `nautilus_trader.core.is_pycapsule(value)`    | `isinstance(value, ExpectedModelType)`        |
209	| `model.as_pycapsule()`                        | Pass the model object                         |
210	| `OrderBookDeltas.from_pycapsule(capsule)`     | Use the `OrderBookDeltas` object directly     |
211	| Databento `load_*_as_pycapsule(...)`          | Call the corresponding `load_*(...)` method   |
212	| Adapter callbacks receiving `PyCapsule`       | Handle the typed model object                 |
213	| `BacktestEngine.add_data` with duck typing    | Pass supported NautilusTrader model objects   |
214	| Duck-typed portfolio-statistic position input | Pass `nautilus_trader.model.Position` objects |
215	
216	`DataQueryResult` iteration returns list chunks containing typed Python objects. Use `to_list()` to
217	flatten all remaining chunks. Query and decode failures raise `RuntimeError` instead of appearing as
218	an exhausted iterator.
219	
220	### Enum absence and side names
221	
222	`AggressorSide.BUYER` and `AggressorSide.SELLER` become `AggressorSide.BUY` and
223	`AggressorSide.SELL`. String, serde, and PostgreSQL output also use `BUY` and `SELL`; legacy
224	`BUYER` and `SELLER` input remains deprecated compatibility input.
225	
226	These Python compatibility attributes now evaluate to `None`, not enum members:
227	
228	- `OrderSide.NO_ORDER_SIDE`
229	- `PositionSide.NO_POSITION_SIDE`
230	- `ContingencyType.NO_CONTINGENCY`
231	- `TrailingOffsetType.NO_TRAILING_OFFSET`
232	- `TriggerType.NO_TRIGGER`
233	
234	Use `is None` for absence checks. The legacy `NO_*` string tokens still parse to `None`, but the
235	attributes no longer have enum properties such as `.name` or `.value` and do not appear in
236	`variants()`.
237	
238	This absence also reaches affected return values. `BookOrder.side`, `DatabentoImbalance.side`,
239	`OrderStatusReport.order_side`, `OrderStatusReport.contingency_type`, and
240	`OrderStatusReport.trailing_offset_type` can return `None`. The concrete order classes also return
241	`None` from `closing_side(PositionSide.FLAT)`. Handle the optional value before accessing enum
242	properties, and use `OrderBookDelta.clear(...)` when constructing a clear delta.
243	
244	### Inspection and state renames
245	
246	V2 exposes consistent read-only inspection across economic instrument types. Properties include
247	`asset_class`, `instrument_class`, currencies, fees, margins, quantity and price limits,
248	`multiplier`, and `tick_scheme`; values may be `None` or a documented default.
249	`SyntheticInstrument` is formula-derived, so inspect its `id`, `components`, `formula`, price
250	precision and increment, and timestamps instead.
251	
252	Several v1 inspection names have direct v2 replacements:
253	
254	| v1 name                                        | v2 name                    |
255	| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
256	| `instrument.tick_scheme_name`                  | `instrument.tick_scheme`   |
257	| `AdaptiveMovingAverage.period` or `.period_er` | `.period_efficiency_ratio` |
258	| `AdaptiveMovingAverage.period_alpha_fast`      | `.period_fast`             |
259	| `AdaptiveMovingAverage.period_alpha_slow`      | `.period_slow`             |
260	| `LinearRegression.R2`                          | `LinearRegression.r2`      |
261	| `DirectionalMovement.value`                    | `.pos` and `.neg`          |
262	| `DataType.type`                                | `DataType.type_name`       |
263	| `Bar.is_revision`                              | removed                    |
264	
265	V1 `DirectionalMovement.value` never changed from zero, so v2 exposes the meaningful positive and
266	negative outputs instead.
267	
268	`MarginAccount.margin()`, `MarginAccount.margins()`, and `MarginAccount.account_margins()` keep
269	their v1 names. Other read-only margin queries move the measure or scope qualifier to the front in
270	v2: for example, `margin_init()` becomes `initial_margin()`, and `margin_init_for_currency()`
271	becomes `account_initial_margin()`.
272	
273	| v1 name                       | v2 name                         |
274	| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
275	| `margin_init()`               | `initial_margin()`              |
276	| `margins_init()`              | `initial_margins()`             |
277	| `margin_maint()`              | `maintenance_margin()`          |
278	| `margins_maint()`             | `maintenance_margins()`         |
279	| `margin_for_currency()`       | `account_margin()`              |
280	| `margin_init_for_currency()`  | `account_initial_margin()`      |
281	| `margin_maint_for_currency()` | `account_maintenance_margin()`  |
282	| `account_margins_init()`      | `account_initial_margins()`     |
283	| `account_margins_maint()`     | `account_maintenance_margins()` |
284	| `total_margin_init()`         | `total_initial_margin()`        |
285	| `total_margin_maint()`        | `total_maintenance_margin()`    |
286	
287	The v2 Python query surface exposes only the read-only methods above. It does not bind the Rust
288	engine mutation methods `update_margin`, `clear_margin`, `clear_account_margin`,
289	`clear_initial_margin`, `clear_maintenance_margin`, or `set_margin_model`. This v2 boundary does
290	not describe which command APIs were available in v1. Existing v2 Python methods, including
291	`update_initial_margin`, `update_maintenance_margin`, `set_default_leverage`, and `set_leverage`,
292	remain unchanged.
293	
294	The payload on `nautilus_trader.model.CustomData` remains available through `.data`. The separate
295	`nautilus_trader.common.CustomData` byte container exposes `.value`; it is not the type accepted by
296	`DataActor.publish_data()`.
297	
298	### Config readback and sensitive values
299	
300	V2 immutable configs expose non-secret constructor values as read-only properties. This includes
301	engine, backtest venue and run, live reconciliation, and data/execution tester settings.
302	`LiveRiskEngineConfig.max_notional_per_order` returns v2's validated strings even when constructed
303	from Python integers or decimal values.
304	
305	Potential credentials use bounded inspection properties instead of raw readback:
306	
307	| Constructor field                                    | Inspection property                   |
308	| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
309	| `BacktestDataConfig.catalog_fs_storage_options`      | `catalog_fs_storage_option_keys`      |
310	| `BacktestDataConfig.catalog_fs_rust_storage_options` | `catalog_fs_rust_storage_option_keys` |
311	
312	These raw fields and adapter credentials remain private. Some configs provide `has_*` checks for
313	credential-bearing proxy, database, or gateway settings without returning their values. Keep
314	secrets in application-owned state if they must be reused.
315	
316	Betfair configuration moves and flattens in v2:
317	
318	- `BetfairDataClientConfig` remains the data factory input, while `BetfairExecClientConfig` becomes
319	  `BetfairExecutionClientConfig`.
320	- `BetfairInstrumentProviderConfig` no longer exists as a separate config. Its
321	  `account_currency`, `default_min_notional`, `event_type_ids`, `event_type_names`, `event_ids`,
322	  `market_ids`, `country_codes`, `market_types`, `min_market_start_time`, and
323	  `max_market_start_time` fields move directly onto `BetfairDataClientConfig`.
324	- Execution reconciliation uses `BetfairExecutionClientConfig.reconcile_market_ids` directly.
325	  `reconcile_market_ids_only` still controls whether the filter applies.
326	- Rename `stream_heartbeat_ms` to `stream_heartbeat_secs` and `stream_idle_timeout_ms` to
327	  `stream_heartbeat_timeout_secs`, then convert configured values from milliseconds to seconds.
328	- `certs_dir` is removed because v2 uses interactive login. The HTTP keepalive interval is fixed
329	  internally at 36,000 seconds rather than exposed as `keep_alive_secs`.
330	
331	Databento configuration also changes shape:
332	
333	- `DatabentoDataClientConfig` remains the factory input. It keeps
334	  `use_exchange_as_venue`, `bars_timestamp_on_close`, and `venue_dataset_map`, adds the required
335	  `publishers_filepath`, and accepts `api_key` as a private constructor value.
336	- The v1 startup preload fields `instrument_ids` and `parent_symbols` are removed. V2 handles live
337	  subscriptions and historical instrument requests directly instead of configuring an instrument
338	  provider preload.
339	- `http_gateway`, `live_gateway`, `timeout_initial_load`, `mbo_subscriptions_delay`, and
340	  `reconnect_timeout_mins` are not accepted by the Python `DatabentoDataClientConfig` constructor.
341	  Reconnection remains an internal client concern; do not copy those v1 fields into current config
342	  construction.
343	
344	Bybit's `bybit_bar_spec_to_interval` now takes a `BarAggregation` and step instead of the
345	aggregation's integer value and step.
346	
347	Interactive Brokers legacy mutation fields have constructor or builder replacements:
348	
349	| V1 field or alias         | V2 replacement                                                                  |
350	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
351	| `legacy_market_data_type` | Pass `market_data_type` to `InteractiveBrokersDataClientConfig`.                |
352	| `legacy_load_ids`         | Pass `load_ids` to `InteractiveBrokersInstrumentProviderConfig`.                |
353	| `legacy_load_contracts`   | Pass `load_contracts` to the instrument provider config.                        |
354	| `legacy_symbology_method` | Pass `symbology_method` to the instrument provider config.                      |
355	| `pickle_path`             | Pass or set `cache_path` on the instrument provider config.                     |
356	| `routing`                 | Pass `RoutingConfig` to `LiveNodeBuilder.add_data_client` or `add_exec_client`. |
357	| `dockerized_gateway`      | Start the gateway outside v2, then pass its `host` and `port`.                  |
358	
359	V2 retains writable `instrument_provider` fields on the data and execution client configs and
360	`cache_path` on the provider config. A non-`None` `dockerized_gateway` is rejected because Python
361	v2 does not own the container lifecycle.
362	
363	Core config types remain grouped under `nautilus_trader.config`. Adapter configs move to the
364	adapter's public module, such as `nautilus_trader.adapters.databento`.
365	
366	The core config names change as follows:
367	
368	| v1 config             | v2 config                  |
369	| --------------------- | -------------------------- |
370	| `ActorConfig`         | `DataActorConfig`          |
371	| `ExecAlgorithmConfig` | `ExecutionAlgorithmConfig` |
372	| `ExecEngineConfig`    | `ExecutionEngineConfig`    |
373	| `LoggingConfig`       | `LoggerConfig`             |
374	| `TradingNodeConfig`   | `LiveNodeConfig`           |
375	
376	Import the current names from `nautilus_trader.config`. `ControllerConfig` has no
377	direct replacement: define controller fields on a `DataActorConfig` subclass, then refer to that
378	class through `ImportableControllerConfig`.
379	
380	V2 uses `Execution` in project-owned type names and omits `Live` from ordinary client names. This
381	changes these public names:
382	
383	| v1 or earlier v2 name           | v2 name                              |
384	| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
385	| `<Venue>ExecClientConfig`       | `<Venue>ExecutionClientConfig`       |
386	| `BetfairDataConfig`             | `BetfairDataClientConfig`            |
387	| `BetfairExecConfig`             | `BetfairExecutionClientConfig`       |
388	| `DatabentoLiveClientConfig`     | `DatabentoDataClientConfig`          |
389	| `LiveDataClientConfig`          | `DataClientConfig`                   |
390	| `LiveExecClientConfig`          | `ExecutionClientConfig`              |
391	| `LiveExecEngineConfig`          | `LiveExecutionEngineConfig`          |
392	| `ImportableExecAlgorithmConfig` | `ImportableExecutionAlgorithmConfig` |
393	| `ExecFactoryExtractor`          | `ExecutionFactoryExtractor`          |
394	| `SimExecFactoryExtractor`       | `SimulatedExecutionFactoryExtractor` |
395	
396	`ExecAlgorithmId`, its associated `exec_*` fields, and `ExecTester` retain their established
397	names. Venue protocol terms such as `ExecType` also remain unchanged. The extractor aliases are
398	Rust extension APIs under `nautilus_system::python::registry`.
399	
400	V2 removes component and client collections from node configuration. Register them explicitly:
401	
402	| v1 config field                        | v2 migration                                                           |
403	| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
404	| `NautilusKernelConfig.message_bus`     | Pass `msgbus` to `BacktestEngineConfig` or `LiveNodeConfig`.           |
405	| `NautilusKernelConfig.actors`          | Call `add_actor` or `add_actor_from_config` on the node.               |
406	| `NautilusKernelConfig.strategies`      | Call `add_strategy` or `add_strategy_from_config` on the node.         |
407	| `NautilusKernelConfig.exec_algorithms` | Call `add_exec_algorithm` or `add_exec_algorithm_from_config`.         |
408	| `TradingNodeConfig.data_clients`       | Call `LiveNodeBuilder.add_data_client`.                                |
409	| `TradingNodeConfig.exec_clients`       | Call `LiveNodeBuilder.add_exec_client` or `add_simulated_exec_client`. |
410	
411	On `LiveNodeConfig`, timeout names now state their unit and the post-stop wait is a delay:
412	
413	| v1 field                 | v2 `LiveNodeConfig` field     |
414	| ------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
415	| `timeout_connection`     | `timeout_connection_secs`     |
416	| `timeout_reconciliation` | `timeout_reconciliation_secs` |
417	| `timeout_portfolio`      | `timeout_portfolio_secs`      |
418	| `timeout_disconnection`  | `timeout_disconnection_secs`  |
419	| `timeout_post_stop`      | `delay_post_stop_secs`        |
420	| `timeout_shutdown`       | `timeout_shutdown_secs`       |
421	
422	`BacktestEngineConfig` keeps the v1 timeout names without the `_secs` suffix, except that
423	`timeout_post_stop` becomes `delay_post_stop`.
424	
425	Execution factories now consume the corresponding execution client config directly. Remove
426	`BitmexExecFactoryConfig`, `DeriveExecFactoryConfig`, and `HyperliquidExecFactoryConfig` wrappers,
427	and pass `BitmexExecutionClientConfig`, `DeriveExecutionClientConfig`, or
428	`HyperliquidExecutionClientConfig` to `add_exec_client`.
429	
430	The live node owns the trader identity. Remove `trader_id` from adapter execution client config
431	construction; `LiveNodeConfig` or `LiveNode.builder(...)` supplies it to every execution factory.
432	Keep the venue-specific `account_id` on the execution client config. The Bybit, Coinbase, and
433	Interactive Brokers execution factories now use no-argument constructors. Custom Rust execution
434	factories must accept `TraderId` in their `ExecutionClientFactory::create` or
435	`SimulatedExecutionClientFactory::create` implementation.
436	
437	`ExecutionClientFactory::create` also requires `clock: Rc<RefCell<dyn Clock>>` after the cache
438	argument, matching `DataClientFactory::create`. Pass the owning node's clock when calling an
439	execution factory directly. `SimulatedExecutionClientFactory` keeps its existing signature.
440	The Python execution client bridge uses the supplied clock. Existing native execution adapters
441	continue to use their realtime clocks internally; this signature change does not add test-clock
442	support to those adapters.
443	
444	The v1 fill, fee, latency, margin, and simulation-module config and factory wrappers are also
445	removed. This includes `Importable*ModelConfig`, `MarginModelConfig`, and their factories, which
446	loaded Python or Cython classes by import path. Construct the current model or module directly,
447	such as `ProbabilisticFillModel`, `FixedFeeModel`, `StaticLatencyModel`, `StandardMarginModel`,
448	`LeveragedMarginModel`, or `FXRolloverInterestModule`, and pass it to the backtest venue.
449	`SimulationModuleConfig` is therefore no longer a separate Python type. Native Rust models are
450	composed at compile time; v1 did not provide runtime native model plugins.
451	
452	`DataCatalogConfig` and `StreamingConfig` have v2-native Python equivalents for `BacktestNode`.
453	Configure existing built-in-data catalog queries and Feather output through `BacktestEngineConfig`.
454	These configs do not restore the v1 factory, download, custom-data, or generic serialization
455	workflows. `DatabaseConfig` has no public v2 Python equivalent. For live trading, configure Redis or
456	Postgres cache backing through `LiveNodeBuilder`; this does not restore the generic v1
457	`DatabaseConfig` workflow. See
458	[cache database configuration](docs/how_to/configure_live_trading.md#cache-database-configuration).
459	
460	Custom Rust cache database adapters used with live orders must implement the batch
461	`index_order_clients` operation. The default trait implementation rejects non-empty claims.
462	
463	The generic Python APIs under `nautilus_trader.network` have no v2 public Python equivalent:
464	`HttpClient`, `HttpMethod`, `HttpResponse`, `SocketClient`, `WebSocketClient`, `SocketConfig`,
465	`WebSocketConfig`, `Quota`, network exceptions, and the `http_*` functions. Adapter-specific
466	low-level Python WebSocket clients and their request, error, and channel-control types are also
467	removed. Use `LiveNode` data and execution clients for streaming venue workflows, retained adapter
468	HTTP clients for supported direct requests, or the Rust `nautilus-network` crate for custom
469	networking. `TransportBackend` remains available from `nautilus_trader.network` only for adapter
470	config transport selection.
471	
472	The v1 `NautilusConfig`, `NautilusKernelConfig`, `ImportableConfig`, config factory classes, and
473	encoding and path utilities are not application config objects in the current package. Use the
474	concrete configs and registration methods instead.
475	
476	Use the generated type stubs in `python/nautilus_trader/` as the supported Python contract. Some
477	adapter wire DTOs expose extra runtime attributes that are not part of that contract. The following
478	methods are callable at runtime but absent from the stubs, so static type checkers cannot resolve
479	them:
480	
481	- `KrakenFuturesHttpClient.edit_orders_batch`
482	- `KrakenFuturesHttpClient.submit_orders_batch`
483	- `KrakenSpotHttpClient.submit_orders_batch`
484	
485	See the [Python concept guide](docs/concepts/python.md) for the runtime ownership model and public
486	API boundaries.
487	
488	The [Rust-native Python examples][python-v2-examples] show current live-node builders, adapter factories,
489	strategies, actors, and data/execution testers.
490	
491	Python v2 strategies subclass `Strategy` and override lifecycle or data callbacks:
492	
493	```python
494	from nautilus_trader.config import StrategyConfig
495	from nautilus_trader.trading import Strategy
496	
497	
498	class MyStrategyConfig(StrategyConfig):
499	    pass
500	
501	
502	class MyStrategy(Strategy):
503	    def on_start(self) -> None:
504	        pass
505	```
506	
507	V1 config classes use msgspec `Struct`, while v2 config classes are Rust/PyO3 types. Imports and
508	subclass constructors written for one version do not work unchanged with the other. Annotated
509	custom fields on a v1 `StrategyConfig` subclass do not carry over. In v2, declare them as
510	keyword-only arguments on `__init__`, accept `**_kwargs` so the base keywords pass through, and call
511	`super().__init__()` with no arguments. The PyO3 base reads its own fields in `__new__` from the same
512	call and ignores the ones it does not recognize, so no `__new__` override is needed. Do not reuse a
513	base field name for a custom field. See the
514	[v2 strategy config example][python-v2-strategy-config].
515	
516	### Register actors, strategies, and algorithms
517	
518	V1 node configs contain importable actors, strategies, and execution algorithms. V2 registers each
519	component on the node instead:
520	
521	- For `BacktestNode`, call `node.build()` first. Then pass the run config ID and a constructed
522	  component to `add_actor`, `add_strategy`, or `add_exec_algorithm`, or use the corresponding
523	  `_from_config` method. Call `node.run()` after registration.
524	- For `LiveNode`, register constructed components or importable configs with the same method pairs
525	  before calling `run()` or `run_async()`.
526	
527	`LiveNode.add_actor` accepts constructed Python actor instances. Registration applies the actor's
528	config, derives its ID, and rejects duplicate IDs or registration after the node leaves its idle
529	state.
530	
531	### Backtest node post-run inspection
532	
533	V2 keeps `BacktestNode` engines internal; the v1 `get_engine` and `get_engines` calls are unavailable.
534	For post-run inspection, set `BacktestRunConfig.dispose_on_completion=False`; the `True` default
535	drops engine state. Then pass the run config ID to the node inspection methods:
536	
537	```python
538	config = BacktestRunConfig(..., dispose_on_completion=False)
539	node = BacktestNode([config])
540	results = node.run()
541	
542	cache = node.get_engine_cache(config.id)
543	portfolio = node.get_engine_portfolio(config.id)
544	statistics = portfolio.statistics()
545	fills = node.generate_fills_report(config.id)
546	```
547	
548	These additional reports also take the run config ID first:
549	
550	- `generate_orders_report`
551	- `generate_order_fills_report`
552	- `generate_positions_report`
553	- `generate_account_report`
554	
555	The [getting-started backtest guides](docs/getting_started/index.md) show the current high-level
556	`BacktestNode` and low-level `BacktestEngine` APIs.
557	
558	### Port a custom portfolio statistic
559	
560	Subclass `PortfolioStatistic` from `nautilus_trader.analysis` as in v1 and register it on the
561	Portfolio rather than on an analyzer. The class name still derives the statistic name, so
562	`MyCustomRatio` registers as "My Custom Ratio" exactly as it did in v1.
563	
564	```python
565	from nautilus_trader.analysis import PortfolioStatistic
566	
567	
568	class TradeCount(PortfolioStatistic):
569	    def calculate_from_realized_pnls(self, realized_pnls: list[float]) -> float | None:
570	        return float(len(realized_pnls))
571	
572	
573	engine.portfolio.register_statistic(TradeCount())
574	```
575	
576	Two changes affect a ported class:
577	
578	- v1 passed `pd.Series`; v2 passes `dict[int, float]` keyed by UNIX nanoseconds for returns and
579	  `list[float]` for realized PnLs. Rewrite any Series-specific code.
580	- `calculate_from_orders` is gone. No v1 or v2 analyzer ever supplied order data to it, so a v1
581	  implementation of that method never ran.
582	
583	The protected `_check_valid_returns` and `_downsample_to_daily_bins` helpers and the
584	`fully_qualified_name()` classmethod have no v2 equivalent. Registrations reach
585	`Portfolio.statistics()`, `BacktestResult`, and the post-run analysis log, and survive repeated
586	queries and analyzer resets. See [Custom statistics](docs/concepts/portfolio.md#custom-statistics).
587	
588	### Live node inspection and host-loop integration
589	
590	V2 exposes the Rust-owned cache and portfolio through `node.cache` and `node.portfolio`. These
591	shared wrappers provide normal inspection without exposing runtime internals.
592	
593	Choose the lifecycle method based on who owns the loop:
594	
595	| Method                  | Contract                                                                                |
596	| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
597	| `LiveNode.run()`        | Runs on the calling thread, owns signal handling, and blocks until shutdown.            |
598	| `LiveNode.run_async()`  | Runs on the caller's asyncio loop and resolves once the node has stopped.               |
599	| `LiveNodeHandle.stop()` | Requests graceful shutdown and returns immediately; the active run completes afterward. |
600	
601	Earlier v2 `LiveNode.start()` and `LiveNode.poll()` no longer exist. Replace an owned-loop start/poll
602	sequence with `run()`, or await `run_async()` when the application owns the event loop.
603	
604	Both entry points run the same lifecycle, so a hosted node performs the same startup ordering,
605	maintenance, external message-bus ingress, reconciliation, and shutdown as an owned one. A host
606	that owns its loop awaits `run_async()` and stops the node through its handle. It must wait for the
607	handle to report `Running`, supervise the run task for unexpected completion, await graceful
608	shutdown, and then dispose the node.
609	
610	Capture `cache`, `portfolio`, and `handle()` before starting, because `run_async()` lends the node
611	to the returned coroutine for the run's duration. Use `LiveNodeHandle.stop()` as the external stop
612	path while either execution mode owns the node. See the
613	[live trading](docs/concepts/live.md#hosted-event-loops) concept guide for the canonical recipe and
614	full contract.
615	
616	### Order factory configuration readback
617	
618	`OrderFactory.trader_id` and `strategy_id` remain available. For the v1
619	`use_uuid_client_order_ids` and `use_hyphens_in_client_order_ids` flags, read `Strategy.config` in a
620	v2 strategy. Standalone factories provide no equivalent flag readback; retain those values in
621	application configuration if needed.
622	
623	### Execution algorithms
624	
625	Python v2 `ExecutionAlgorithm` remains a routed-order component rather than inheriting the full
626	`Actor` authoring surface. Supported override points include:
627	
628	- `on_order`
629	- `on_order_list`
630	- Order and position callbacks
631	- Lifecycle callbacks
632	- `on_signal`
633	
634	The runtime owns command routing and calls `execute`; do not call or override `execute` as the
635	algorithm entrypoint.
636	
637	An execution algorithm cannot submit a spawned order with a live emulation trigger. Use
638	`emulation_trigger=None`; Python raises `ValueError` if `submit_order` receives a triggered child.
639	After a failed spawn with `reduce_primary=True`, discard or refresh the caller-held primary order:
640	quantity restoration updates the cached primary order.
641	
642	V2 `OrderList` stores client order IDs instead of order objects. The runtime resolves those IDs
643	through the cache and calls `on_order_list(order_list, orders)`, where `orders` follows the client
644	order ID order. If the subclass overrides `on_order_list`, it receives one list callback and the
645	runtime does not also call `on_order`. Without an override, the default implementation calls
646	`on_order` once for each resolved order. Change v1 one-argument overrides to accept `orders`; the
647	v1 default did not fan out order lists.
648	
649	The supported authoring surface has these v1 dispositions:
650	
651	| V1 `ExecAlgorithm` / `Actor` capability | Python v2 contract                                                                |
652	| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
653	| `cache`                                 | Available as a read-only property after node or engine registration.              |
654	| `portfolio`                             | Available as a read-only property after node or engine registration.              |
655	| `greeks`                                | Construct `GreeksCalculator(self.cache, self.clock)` after registration.          |
656	| `msgbus`                                | Use component topic methods for Python objects or signals for lightweight values. |
657	| Registered indicators                   | Use `DataActor` or `Strategy` for indicator-driven workflows.                     |
658	| Market-data subscriptions and callbacks | Use `DataActor` or `Strategy`; algorithms inspect cache and routed events.        |
659	| Lifecycle state and control             | Use `is_*()` and lifecycle methods; the Rust component remains authoritative.     |
660	| Direct `register(...)`                  | Use `BacktestEngine.add_exec_algorithm` or `LiveNode.add_exec_algorithm`.         |
661	
662	Python v2 `DataActor`, `Strategy`, and `ExecutionAlgorithm` expose `publish_message(topic, message)`,
663	`subscribe_topic(topic, handler, priority=0)`, and `unsubscribe_topic(topic, handler)` for arbitrary
664	in-process Python objects. Handlers receive the original object synchronously, and subscriptions
665	belong to the subscribing component. See [Python topic messaging](docs/concepts/message_bus.md#python-topic-messaging)
666	for callable identity, lifecycle, and thread requirements.
667	
668	For lightweight signals:
669	
670	- Call `subscribe_signal(name)` during `on_start`.
671	- Handle `on_signal(signal)`.
672	- Call `publish_signal(name, value)`.
673	
674	Signal values use their string representation. Raw message-bus endpoint registration remains
675	a runtime internal API.
676	
677	```python
678	from nautilus_trader.common import GreeksCalculator
679	from nautilus_trader.trading import ExecutionAlgorithm
680	
681	
682	class RoutedAlgorithm(ExecutionAlgorithm):
683	    def on_start(self) -> None:
684	        self._greeks = GreeksCalculator(self.cache, self.clock)
685	        self.subscribe_signal("execution-control")
686	
687	    def on_signal(self, signal) -> None:
688	        self.log.info(f"Received {signal.value}")
689	
690	    def on_order(self, order) -> None:
691	        instrument = self.cache.instrument(order.instrument_id)
692	        portfolio_ready = self.portfolio.is_initialized()
693	        self.log.info(f"Routing {instrument.id}; portfolio ready={portfolio_ready}")
694	```
695	
696	Order `exec_algorithm_params` keys and values remain string-only across the v2 model and Python
697	bindings. Encode each value as a string when constructing the order, then parse it in the algorithm.
698	For example, pass `exec_algorithm_params={"horizon_secs": "300", "interval_secs": "10"}`, not
699	numeric values. This keeps Python authoring aligned with the Rust `IndexMap<Ustr, Ustr>` contract.
700	
701	`ExecutionAlgorithmConfig` supports Python subclasses with custom fields. The inherited
702	`__new__` applies the base fields before the Python `__init__` runs, so the subclass initializes
703	only its custom attributes. Declare those fields keyword-only and keep `**_kwargs` so the subclass
704	accepts the base keywords. The base constructor ignores other unmatched keywords, so validate
705	optional custom inputs in `__init__`.
706	
707	```python
708	from nautilus_trader.config import ExecutionAlgorithmConfig
709	from nautilus_trader.model import ExecAlgorithmId
710	
711	
712	class RoutedAlgorithmConfig(ExecutionAlgorithmConfig):
713	    def __init__(
714	        self,
715	        *,
716	        horizon_secs: str,
717	        interval_secs: str,
718	        **_kwargs,
719	    ) -> None:
720	        super().__init__()
721	        self.horizon_secs = horizon_secs
722	        self.interval_secs = interval_secs
723	
724	
725	config = RoutedAlgorithmConfig(
726	    exec_algorithm_id=ExecAlgorithmId("ROUTED"),
727	    horizon_secs="300",
728	    interval_secs="10",
729	    log_events=False,
730	)
731	algorithm = RoutedAlgorithm(config)
732	```
733	
734	If an algorithm subclass defines `__init__`, call `super().__init__(config)` to retain its Python
735	instance and config for export.
736	
737	Define the algorithm and config classes at module scope so the exported import paths resolve.
738	
739	Constructed instances and importable configs work in backtest and live workflows:
740	
741	- Register v2 `ExecutionAlgorithm` instances with `BacktestEngine.add_exec_algorithm` or
742	  `LiveNode.add_exec_algorithm`.
743	- Call `algorithm.to_importable_config()` to export the algorithm path, config path, and config
744	  values.
745	- Register the result with `BacktestEngine.add_exec_algorithm_from_config` or
746	  `LiveNode.add_exec_algorithm_from_config`.
747	- Register DataActor-based compatibility algorithms with `add_exec_algorithm_from_config`.
748	
749	Nodes normally drive lifecycle transitions. Direct lifecycle methods remain available for
750	control-plane integrations and dispatch the same Python callbacks.
751	
752	Port one workflow at a time and verify the generated stub before replacing a v1 convenience method.
753	Do not assume that a v1 adapter config field also exists on its v2 Rust config.
754	
755	## Behavior changes
756	
757	Account for these differences from v1:
758	
759	- V2 `BookLevel` comparisons follow ladder priority: bids sort from highest to lowest price, and
760	  asks sort from lowest to highest. Equality includes the side, and ordering levels from opposite
761	  sides raises `TypeError`. Sort on `level.price` when code needs side-independent price order.
762	- V2 `OrderBook` pickle data is not interchangeable with v1 pickle data. Rebuild snapshots from
763	  source market data when moving between the implementations.
764	- `OrderBookDeltas.is_snapshot` tests `F_SNAPSHOT` on the batch flags, which come from the final
765	  delta. The old implementation tested whether the first delta had a `CLEAR` action, so a clear
766	  without the flag is not a snapshot.
767	- Instrument `activation_utc` and `expiration_utc` properties return UTC-aware `datetime.datetime`
768	  values. Use `activation_ns` and `expiration_ns` when exact nanosecond precision is required.
769	- v2 caches `OptionGreeks` for option fee calculation; this extends v1.
770	- `Bar.is_revision` is not exposed on the v2 Python surface. Do not depend on it during migration.
771	- A direct `Position.apply` fill that crosses zero resets the open entry price to the flipping fill.
772	  v1 retains the old side's entry price; the v2 behavior is the go-forward contract.
773	- `Position.apply` validates the fill's instrument ID, position ID, and ordinary trade-ID uniqueness
774	  before mutation. Invalid fills leave the position unchanged and raise `ValueError`; v1 raises
775	  `KeyError` for a duplicate trade ID and does not validate both identities on every apply.
776	- `PortfolioConfig.use_mark_prices` defaults to `true`; v1 defaulted to `false`. Set it to `false` to
777	  skip mark prices.
778	- `PortfolioAnalyzer.realized_pnls()` returns records in ascending event-time order. V1 returned
779	  position-derived records followed by recorded ones, which was not chronological.
780	- Registered PnL statistics run for every analyzed currency, including runs that closed no trades,
781	  where they receive an empty list. `Win Rate` and its peers therefore report NaN for such runs
782	  rather than being absent.
783	- A portfolio statistic that raises no longer propagates. V2 logs the error and routes it through
784	  `sys.unraisablehook`, because the calculation crosses into Rust where there is no error channel.
785	- Backtest venues no longer accept `settlement_prices`. Add `InstrumentClose` data with
786	  `close_type=InstrumentCloseType.CONTRACT_EXPIRED`; its exact `close_price` settles futures, binary
787	  contracts, and option close legs at expiry.
788	- An omitted backtest `default_leverage` now selects 10x for margin accounts and 1x for cash
789	  accounts. Set `default_leverage=Decimal(1)` to retain v1's unleveraged behavior.
790	- v2 `OrderList` stores client order IDs instead of order objects:
791	  - Use the resolved `orders` argument in `ExecutionAlgorithm.on_order_list(order_list, orders)`.
792	  - Elsewhere, replace `order_list.orders` with `order_list.client_order_ids()`, then resolve each
793	    ID through `cache.order(client_order_id)`.
794	  - Replace `order_list.first` with `cache.order(order_list.first_client_order_id)` after checking
795	    the ID is not `None`.
796	- Catalog order-event data written before `activation_price` and `OrderFilled.info` were added cannot
797	  be read by the new schema. Regenerate or migrate that data before upgrading a catalog in place.
798	- `Order.avg_px` and `Order.slippage` are `decimal.Decimal`, where v1 exposes `float`. v2 no longer
799	  converts the weighted average through `f64`, so comparisons against float literals can fail on a
800	  fractional value: `Decimal("0.70000") == 0.7` is `False`. Compare against `Decimal("0.7")`, or wrap
801	  the operand with `Decimal(str(value))`.
802	- `Order.to_dict()` returns `avg_px` and `slippage` as strings, matching how the other decimal
803	  fields already serialize. Wrap the value in `Decimal(...)` before doing arithmetic on it.
804	
805	### Rust order history
806	
807	Rust callers construct `OrderCore` with `OrderCore::new`, apply events with `OrderCore::apply`, and
808	inspect history with `OrderCore::events()`. Direct field access to `events` and struct-literal
809	construction are no longer available. Use `OrderCore::prepend_events` to retain history when transforming an order;
810	it preserves event order without applying state transitions. Use `OrderAny::from_events` to reconstruct
811	an order from replacement history. The serialized order format is unchanged.
812	
813	### PostgreSQL schema changes
814	
815	Postgres-backed deployments must run `nautilus database init` before starting a v2 node. The
816	`order.avg_px` and `order.slippage` columns move from `double precision` to `NUMERIC`, and the node
817	fails at connect time while the old column types remain.
818	
819	Existing databases whose `AGGRESSOR_SIDE` enum still contains `BUYER` and `SELLER` also need this
820	one-time migration before ingesting v2 data:
821	
822	```sql
823	ALTER TYPE AGGRESSOR_SIDE RENAME VALUE 'BUYER' TO 'BUY';
824	ALTER TYPE AGGRESSOR_SIDE RENAME VALUE 'SELLER' TO 'SELL';
825	```
826	
827	Do not run those statements if the enum already contains `BUY` and `SELL`.
828	
829	## Compare backtest performance
830	
831	Use `scripts/benchmark-backtest-versions.py` for a wall-clock comparison between the released v1
832	Cython engine and the v2 PyO3 engine. The driver owns one shared scenario matrix and normalizes the
833	small API differences at runtime. It rejects a run before timing unless both environments use the
834	expected package version, backend, source revision, Python version, and precision mode. For v2, it
835	also requires the requested source revision to be embedded in the loaded extension.
836	
837	Run the comparison on a quiet host. These commands create isolated release environments and a
838	detached v1 worktree without changing the current branch:
839	
840	```bash
841	COMPARE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/nautilus-backtest-compare.XXXXXX)
842	git worktree add --detach "$COMPARE_ROOT/v1" v1.231.0
843	
844	uv venv --python /usr/bin/python3.12 "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v1"
845	(
846	    cd "$COMPARE_ROOT/v1"
847	    uvx --from uv==0.11.33 uv build --wheel --python /usr/bin/python3.12 \
848	        --out-dir "$COMPARE_ROOT/wheels-v1"
849	)
850	V1_WHEEL=$(find "$COMPARE_ROOT/wheels-v1" -type f -name 'nautilus_trader-*.whl')
851	UV_LINK_MODE=copy uv pip install --no-cache \
852	    --python "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v1/bin/python" "$V1_WHEEL"
853	
854	uv venv --python /usr/bin/python3.12 "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v2"
855	uv pip install --python "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v2/bin/python" maturin==1.14.1 patchelf
856	(
857	    cd python
858	    CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=16 "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v2/bin/maturin" build --release \
859	        --out "$COMPARE_ROOT/wheels-v2"
860	)
861	V2_WHEEL=$(find "$COMPARE_ROOT/wheels-v2" -type f -name 'nautilus_trader-*.whl')
862	UV_LINK_MODE=copy uv pip install --no-cache \
863	    --python "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v2/bin/python" "$V2_WHEEL"
864	
865	V1_COMMIT=$(git -C "$COMPARE_ROOT/v1" rev-parse HEAD)
866	V2_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
867	python3.12 scripts/benchmark-backtest-versions.py compare \
868	    --v1-python "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v1/bin/python" \
869	    --v1-artifact "$V1_WHEEL" \
870	    --v1-source "$COMPARE_ROOT/v1" \
871	    --v1-commit "$V1_COMMIT" \
872	    --v2-python "$COMPARE_ROOT/env-v2/bin/python" \
873	    --v2-artifact "$V2_WHEEL" \
874	    --v2-source "$PWD" \
875	    --v2-commit "$V2_COMMIT" \
876	    --sessions 5 \
877	    --output "$COMPARE_ROOT/results.json"
878	```
879	
880	The driver runs each boundary in both environments back-to-back and reverses or rotates the case
881	order across sessions. `run_preloaded` times only `BacktestEngine.run()` after fixture creation,
882	engine construction, and data registration. `load_build_run` includes instrument and data fixture
883	creation, engine construction, data registration, and `run()`. The coordinator proves that each
884	loaded extension byte-matches the corresponding wheel member before the run and rechecks the full
885	identities after it. After every timed sample, its worker repeats the complete wheel, extension,
886	source, and runtime identity proof and checks its canonical digest against the coordinator's
887	initial identity. Raw output stores each full identity once and binds every sample to it by digest.
888	Source identity hashes staged diffs, unstaged diffs, and untracked file contents in addition to the
889	revision. Exact event, order, position, and account fingerprints are checked after every timed
890	iteration without adding fingerprint work to the duration.
891	
892	Repeat `--scenario <name>` or `--boundary <name>` on the `compare` command to run a targeted subset.
893	Omit both options to run the complete matrix. Raw output stores one full fingerprint for each
894	selected scenario and boundary, then binds every timed sample to it by digest.
895	
896	The JSON output contains every elapsed sample, the observed host state, boundary definitions,
897	medians, minimum-to-maximum spread, v2/v1 ratios, and percentage gaps. The driver requires at least
898	three full sessions. It records CPU governor and `perf_event_paranoid` values but does not change
899	host controls.
900	
901	## Known limitations
902	
903	These gaps can affect migration but do not block supported cutover workflows:
904	
905	- Python request callbacks do not provide v1 joined-response, pending-request cleanup, or late and
906	  duplicate delivery convenience behavior.
907	- Python v2 accepts built-in backing configs such as `RedisMessageBusConfig`, but arbitrary Python
908	  factory classes remain unsupported. V1
909	  `MessageBusConfig(database=DatabaseConfig(...), external_streams=[...])` maps to the builder calls
910	  `LiveNodeBuilder.with_msgbus_config(...)` and
911	  `LiveNodeBuilder.with_external_msgbus_factory(RedisMessageBusConfig(...))`. See
912	  [live message-bus configuration][live-message-bus-config]. The existing
913	  `RedisMessageBusFactory(RedisMessageBusConfig(...))` wrapper remains supported.
914	- Official in-tree live adapters remain configurable from Python through
915	  `LiveNodeBuilder.add_data_client` and `add_exec_client`. Sandbox simulated execution uses
916	  `add_simulated_exec_client`. A working sandbox client does not mean a custom live factory will
917	  register: neither path currently accepts an out-of-tree Python factory, and v1 `LiveDataClient`
918	  and `LiveExecutionClient` subclassing has no v2 equivalent yet. An out-of-tree Python adapter
919	  surface is planned. See [Python support boundaries][python-support-boundaries] and
920	  [issue 4694][python-v2-out-of-tree-adapters].
921	- The PostgreSQL cache loads positions but not synthetics. It also does not persist actor or strategy
922	  state or write cache heartbeats. Redis backing supports these operations.
923	- External message-bus publishing of serialized order and position snapshots remains deferred.
924	- Python `LiveNodeConfig` does not accept the v1 kernel-level `streaming` or `emulator` fields, and
925	  `loop_debug=True` is rejected by the Rust live runtime. Order emulation itself remains available
926	  through order emulation triggers.
927	- V2 `BacktestNode` catalog configuration does not support v1 data-client factories, a download
928	  engine, on-the-fly downloads, custom data, or data frames.
929	- `BacktestNode` builds its engines internally, so a custom portfolio statistic cannot be registered
930	  before a node run. Use `BacktestEngine` directly when a run needs one.
931	- Instrument-provider filter dictionaries are not a common v2 adapter contract. Hyperliquid v2
932	  loads its configured instrument universe and does not accept the v1 `instrument_provider` field.
933	  Check each adapter's Rust/PyO3 config rather than copying v1 provider examples.
934	
935	The [v2 roadmap][v2-roadmap] tracks the wider post-cutover surface. Release-specific breaking
936	changes remain in [RELEASES.md][release-notes].
937	
938	[live-message-bus-config]: docs/how_to/configure_live_trading.md#messagebus-configuration
939	[python-support-boundaries]: docs/concepts/python.md#support-boundaries
940	[python-v2-examples]: examples/README.md#live-adapter-examples
941	[python-v2-out-of-tree-adapters]: https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4694
942	[python-v2-strategy-config]: python/tests/strategies/ema_cross.py
943	[release-notes]: RELEASES.md
944	[v2-roadmap]: https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4042
945

````text
     1	# Run a Backtest (Rust)
     2	
     3	Nautilus provides two Rust APIs for backtesting: `BacktestEngine`
     4	(low-level) and `BacktestNode` (high-level with catalog streaming). This
     5	guide covers both.
     6	
     7	For background on backtesting concepts, fill models, and matching engine
     8	behavior, see the [Backtesting](../concepts/backtesting/) concept guide.
     9	For project setup and feature flags, see the
    10	[Rust](../concepts/rust.md#project-setup) concept guide.
    11	
    12	## Dependencies
    13	
    14	Add the following to your `Cargo.toml`. The `streaming` and
    15	`nautilus-persistence` entries are only needed for the high-level
    16	`BacktestNode` API.
    17	
    18	```toml
    19	[dependencies]
    20	nautilus-backtest = { version = "0.63", features = ["streaming"] }
    21	nautilus-execution = "0.63"
    22	nautilus-model = { version = "0.63", features = ["test-support"] }
    23	nautilus-persistence = "0.63"
    24	nautilus-trading = { version = "0.63", features = ["examples"] }
    25	
    26	ahash = "0.8"
    27	anyhow = "1"
    28	tempfile = "3"
    29	ustr = "1"
    30	```
    31	
    32	If you only need the low-level `BacktestEngine`, drop `streaming`,
    33	`nautilus-persistence`, `tempfile`, and `ustr`.
    34	
    35	## BacktestEngine (low-level API)
    36	
    37	The low-level API gives direct control: you build the engine, add venues and
    38	instruments, load data in memory, register strategies, and run.
    39	
    40	### 1. Create the engine
    41	
    42	```rust
    43	use nautilus_backtest::{config::BacktestEngineConfig, engine::BacktestEngine};
    44	
    45	let mut engine = BacktestEngine::new(BacktestEngineConfig::default())?;
    46	```
    47	
    48	### 2. Add a venue
    49	
    50	`SimulatedVenueConfig` uses a `bon::Builder`: only required fields must be set,
    51	every other setting falls back to a documented default. `build()` validates the
    52	configuration and returns a `ConfigResult`, so propagate or unwrap it.
    53	
    54	```rust
    55	use nautilus_backtest::config::SimulatedVenueConfig;
    56	use nautilus_model::{
    57	    enums::{AccountType, BookType, OmsType},
    58	    identifiers::Venue,
    59	    types::Money,
    60	};
    61	
    62	engine.add_venue(
    63	    SimulatedVenueConfig::builder()
    64	        .venue(Venue::from("SIM"))
    65	        .oms_type(OmsType::Hedging)
    66	        .account_type(AccountType::Margin)
    67	        .book_type(BookType::L1_MBP)
    68	        .starting_balances(vec![Money::from("1_000_000 USD")])
    69	        .build()?,
    70	)?;
    71	```
    72	
    73	Override any default by chaining setters, e.g. `.reject_stop_orders(false)` or
    74	`.allow_cash_borrowing(true)`.
    75	
    76	### 3. Add instruments and data
    77	
    78	```rust
    79	use nautilus_model::instruments::{
    80	    Instrument, InstrumentAny, stubs::audusd_sim,
    81	};
    82	
    83	let instrument = InstrumentAny::CurrencyPair(audusd_sim());
    84	let instrument_id = instrument.id();
    85	engine.add_instrument(&instrument)?;
    86	
    87	let quotes = generate_quotes(instrument_id); // Your data loading function
    88	engine.add_data(quotes, None, true, true)?;
    89	```
    90	
    91	### 4. Register a strategy and run
    92	
    93	```rust
    94	use nautilus_model::types::Quantity;
    95	use nautilus_trading::examples::strategies::EmaCross;
    96	
    97	let strategy = EmaCross::new(
    98	    instrument_id,
    99	    Quantity::from("100000"),
   100	    10, // fast EMA period
   101	    20, // slow EMA period
   102	);
   103	
   104	engine.add_strategy(strategy)?;
   105	engine.run(None, None, None, false)?;
   106	```
   107	
   108	### Run the full example
   109	
   110	```bash
   111	cargo run -p nautilus-backtest --features examples --example engine-ema-cross
   112	```
   113	
   114	Source:
   115	[`crates/backtest/examples/engine_ema_cross.rs`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/backtest/examples/engine_ema_cross.rs)
   116	
   117	## BacktestNode (high-level API)
   118	
   119	The high-level API loads data from a `ParquetDataCatalog` and streams in
   120	configurable chunk sizes. Requires the `streaming` feature on
   121	`nautilus-backtest`.
   122	
   123	### 1. Write data to a catalog
   124	
   125	```rust
   126	use nautilus_model::instruments::{
   127	    Instrument, InstrumentAny, stubs::audusd_sim,
   128	};
   129	use nautilus_persistence::backend::catalog::ParquetDataCatalog;
   130	use tempfile::TempDir;
   131	
   132	let instrument = InstrumentAny::CurrencyPair(audusd_sim());
   133	let instrument_id = instrument.id();
   134	let quotes = generate_quotes(instrument_id);
   135	
   136	let temp_dir = TempDir::new()?;
   137	let catalog_path = temp_dir.path().to_str()
   138	    .context("temp dir path is not valid UTF-8")?
   139	    .to_string();
   140	let catalog = ParquetDataCatalog::new(
   141	    temp_dir.path(), None, None, None, None,
   142	);
   143	
   144	catalog.write_instruments(vec![instrument])?;
   145	catalog.write_to_parquet(&quotes, None, None, None)?;
   146	```
   147	
   148	### 2. Configure the run
   149	
   150	```rust
   151	use nautilus_backtest::config::{
   152	    BacktestDataConfig, BacktestRunConfig, BacktestVenueConfig, NautilusDataType,
   153	};
   154	use nautilus_model::enums::{AccountType, BookType, OmsType};
   155	
   156	let venue_config = BacktestVenueConfig::builder()
   157	    .name("SIM")
   158	    .oms_type(OmsType::Hedging)
   159	    .account_type(AccountType::Margin)
   160	    .book_type(BookType::L1_MBP)
   161	    .starting_balances(vec!["1_000_000 USD".to_string()])
   162	    .build()?;
   163	
   164	let data_config = BacktestDataConfig::builder()
   165	    .data_type(NautilusDataType::QuoteTick)
   166	    .catalog_path(catalog_path)
   167	    .instrument_id(instrument_id)
   168	    .build()?;
   169	
   170	let run_config = BacktestRunConfig::builder()
   171	    .id("ema-cross-run".to_string())
   172	    .venues(vec![venue_config])
   173	    .data(vec![data_config])
   174	    .chunk_size(100)
   175	    .build()?;
   176	```
   177	
   178	### 3. Build, add strategies, and run
   179	
   180	```rust
   181	use nautilus_backtest::node::BacktestNode;
   182	use nautilus_model::types::Quantity;
   183	use nautilus_trading::examples::strategies::EmaCross;
   184	
   185	let mut node = BacktestNode::new(vec![run_config])?;
   186	node.build()?;
   187	
   188	let engine = node.get_engine_mut("ema-cross-run")
   189	    .context("engine not found for run config ID")?;
   190	let strategy = EmaCross::new(
   191	    instrument_id,
   192	    Quantity::from("100000"),
   193	    10,
   194	    20,
   195	);
   196	engine.add_strategy(strategy)?;
   197	
   198	node.run()?;
   199	```
   200	
   201	### Run the full example
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	cargo run -p nautilus-backtest --features examples,streaming --example node-ema-cross
   205	```
   206	
   207	Source:
   208	[`crates/backtest/examples/node_ema_cross.rs`](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/tree/develop/crates/backtest/examples/node_ema_cross.rs)
````

# %% [markdown]
# # EMA cross
#
# Define the reusable bar-based EMA cross strategy used by the FX bars tutorial.

# %%
from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import Decimal

from nautilus_trader.config import StrategyConfig
from nautilus_trader.indicators import ExponentialMovingAverage
from nautilus_trader.model import Bar
from nautilus_trader.model import BarType
from nautilus_trader.model import InstrumentId
from nautilus_trader.model import OrderSide
from nautilus_trader.trading import Strategy


class EMACrossConfig(StrategyConfig):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        instrument_id: InstrumentId,
        bar_type: BarType,
        trade_size: Decimal,
        fast_ema_period: int = 10,
        slow_ema_period: int = 20,
        **_kwargs: object,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.instrument_id = instrument_id
        self.bar_type = bar_type
        self.trade_size = trade_size
        self.fast_ema_period = fast_ema_period
        self.slow_ema_period = slow_ema_period


class EMACross(Strategy):
    def __init__(self, config: EMACrossConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__(config)
        self.fast_ema = ExponentialMovingAverage(config.fast_ema_period)
        self.slow_ema = ExponentialMovingAverage(config.slow_ema_period)

    def on_start(self) -> None:
        self.register_indicator_for_bars(self.config.bar_type, self.fast_ema)
        self.register_indicator_for_bars(self.config.bar_type, self.slow_ema)
        self.subscribe_bars(self.config.bar_type)

    def on_bar(self, _bar: Bar) -> None:
        if not self.indicators_initialized():
            return

        if self.fast_ema.value >= self.slow_ema.value:
            if self.portfolio.is_net_flat(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.buy()
            elif self.portfolio.is_net_short(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)
                self.buy()
        elif self.fast_ema.value < self.slow_ema.value:
            if self.portfolio.is_net_flat(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.sell()
            elif self.portfolio.is_net_long(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)
                self.sell()

    def buy(self) -> None:
        instrument = self.cache.instrument(self.config.instrument_id)
        order = self.order_factory.market(
            self.config.instrument_id,
            OrderSide.BUY,
            instrument.make_qty(self.config.trade_size),
        )
        self.submit_order(order)

    def sell(self) -> None:
        instrument = self.cache.instrument(self.config.instrument_id)
        order = self.order_factory.market(
            self.config.instrument_id,
            OrderSide.SELL,
            instrument.make_qty(self.config.trade_size),
        )
        self.submit_order(order)

    def on_stop(self) -> None:
        self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)

# %% [markdown]
# # Backtest (Low-Level API)
#
# Use `BacktestEngine` for direct component access: load market data, wire up
# strategies and execution algorithms, and run backtests with full control over
# every step. This tutorial backtests an EMA cross strategy with a TWAP execution
# algorithm on a simulated Binance Spot exchange using historical trade tick data.
#
# [View source on GitHub](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/blob/develop/docs/getting_started/backtest_low_level.py).

# %% [markdown]
# ## Prerequisites
# - Python 3.12+
# - [NautilusTrader](https://pypi.org/project/nautilus_trader/) 2.x installed
#   (`pip install -U --pre nautilus_trader`). The `--pre` flag is required while 2.x
#   ships as `2.0.0rcN`.
# - pandas (`pip install pandas`), used by the reports at the end. The wheel
#   declares no runtime dependencies.

# %%
from decimal import Decimal

from nautilus_trader.backtest import BacktestEngine
from nautilus_trader.common import LogLevel
from nautilus_trader.config import BacktestEngineConfig
from nautilus_trader.config import ExecutionAlgorithmConfig
from nautilus_trader.config import LoggerConfig
from nautilus_trader.config import StrategyConfig
from nautilus_trader.indicators import ExponentialMovingAverage
from nautilus_trader.model import AccountType
from nautilus_trader.model import Bar
from nautilus_trader.model import BarType
from nautilus_trader.model import Currency
from nautilus_trader.model import ExecAlgorithmId
from nautilus_trader.model import InstrumentId
from nautilus_trader.model import Money
from nautilus_trader.model import OmsType
from nautilus_trader.model import OrderSide
from nautilus_trader.model import TraderId
from nautilus_trader.model import Venue
from nautilus_trader.testkit.providers import TestDataProvider
from nautilus_trader.testkit.providers import TestInstrumentProvider
from nautilus_trader.trading import Strategy


# %% [markdown]
# ## Load data
#
# Load bundled test data (ETHUSDT trades from Binance), initialize the matching
# instrument, and build Nautilus `TradeTick` objects from the CSV.

# %%
# Initialize the instrument which matches the data
ETHUSDT_BINANCE = TestInstrumentProvider.ethusdt_binance()

# Build Nautilus trade ticks from the bundled Binance CSV
ticks = TestDataProvider.trades_from_binance_csv(
    ETHUSDT_BINANCE,
    "binance/ethusdt-trades.csv",
)

# %% [markdown]
# See the [Data](../concepts/data/) concept guide for details on the data processing pipeline.

# %% [markdown]
# ## Initialize the engine
#
# Pass a `BacktestEngineConfig` to configure the engine. Here we set a custom
# `trader_id` to show the pattern.

# %%
# Configure backtest engine
config = BacktestEngineConfig(
    trader_id=TraderId("BACKTESTER-001"),
    logging=LoggerConfig(stdout_level=LogLevel.ERROR),
)

# Build the backtest engine
engine = BacktestEngine(config=config)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Add a venue
#
# Set up a simulated venue that matches the market data. Here we configure a
# Binance Spot exchange with a cash account.

# %%
# Add a trading venue (multiple venues possible)
BINANCE = Venue("BINANCE")
engine.add_venue(
    venue=BINANCE,
    oms_type=OmsType.NETTING,
    account_type=AccountType.CASH,  # Spot CASH account (not for perpetuals or futures)
    base_currency=None,  # Multi-currency account
    starting_balances=[
        Money(1_000_000.0, Currency.from_str("USDT")),
        Money(10.0, Currency.from_str("ETH")),
    ],
)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Add data
#
# Add the instrument and trade ticks to the engine.

# %%
# Add instrument(s)
engine.add_instrument(ETHUSDT_BINANCE)

# Add data
engine.add_data(ticks)

# %% [markdown]
# :::note
# You can add multiple data types (including custom types) and backtest across multiple venues.
# :::
#

# %% [markdown]
# ## Add strategies
#
# The strategy extends `Strategy` and trades an EMA crossover on 250-tick bars,
# which the engine aggregates internally from the trade ticks. Entries are
# submitted with an `exec_algorithm_id` so the engine routes them to the TWAP
# execution algorithm for slicing.


# %%
class EMACrossTWAPConfig(StrategyConfig):
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        instrument_id: InstrumentId,
        bar_type: BarType,
        trade_size: Decimal,
        fast_ema_period: int = 10,
        slow_ema_period: int = 20,
        twap_horizon_secs: float = 10.0,
        twap_interval_secs: float = 2.5,
        **_kwargs: object,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.instrument_id = instrument_id
        self.bar_type = bar_type
        self.trade_size = trade_size
        self.fast_ema_period = fast_ema_period
        self.slow_ema_period = slow_ema_period
        self.twap_horizon_secs = twap_horizon_secs
        self.twap_interval_secs = twap_interval_secs


class EMACrossTWAP(Strategy):
    def __init__(self, config: EMACrossTWAPConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__(config)
        self.fast_ema = ExponentialMovingAverage(config.fast_ema_period)
        self.slow_ema = ExponentialMovingAverage(config.slow_ema_period)
        self.exec_algorithm_id = ExecAlgorithmId("TWAP")
        self.exec_algorithm_params = {
            "horizon_secs": str(config.twap_horizon_secs),
            "interval_secs": str(config.twap_interval_secs),
        }

    def on_start(self) -> None:
        self.register_indicator_for_bars(self.config.bar_type, self.fast_ema)
        self.register_indicator_for_bars(self.config.bar_type, self.slow_ema)
        self.subscribe_bars(self.config.bar_type)

    def on_bar(self, _bar: Bar) -> None:
        if not self.indicators_initialized():
            return

        if self.fast_ema.value >= self.slow_ema.value:
            if self.portfolio.is_net_flat(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.buy()
            elif self.portfolio.is_net_short(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)
                self.buy()
        elif self.fast_ema.value < self.slow_ema.value:
            if self.portfolio.is_net_flat(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.sell()
            elif self.portfolio.is_net_long(self.config.instrument_id):
                self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)
                self.sell()

    def buy(self) -> None:
        self.submit_twap_order(OrderSide.BUY)

    def sell(self) -> None:
        self.submit_twap_order(OrderSide.SELL)

    def submit_twap_order(self, side: OrderSide) -> None:
        instrument = self.cache.instrument(self.config.instrument_id)
        order = self.order_factory.market(
            self.config.instrument_id,
            side,
            instrument.make_qty(self.config.trade_size),
            exec_algorithm_id=self.exec_algorithm_id,
            exec_algorithm_params=self.exec_algorithm_params,
        )
        self.submit_order(order)

    def on_stop(self) -> None:
        self.close_all_positions(self.config.instrument_id)


# %%
# Configure and add the strategy
strategy_config = EMACrossTWAPConfig(
    instrument_id=ETHUSDT_BINANCE.id,
    bar_type=BarType.from_str("ETHUSDT.BINANCE-250-TICK-LAST-INTERNAL"),
    trade_size=Decimal("0.10"),
    fast_ema_period=10,
    slow_ema_period=20,
    twap_horizon_secs=10.0,
    twap_interval_secs=2.5,
)

strategy = EMACrossTWAP(config=strategy_config)
engine.add_strategy(strategy=strategy)

# %% [markdown]
# The strategy config carries the TWAP parameters, but the execution algorithm
# itself is a separate component.
#
# ## Add execution algorithms
#
# Register the built-in TWAP execution algorithm under the `TWAP` identifier the
# strategy references.

# %%
# Add the native TWAP execution algorithm
engine.add_native_exec_algorithm(
    "TwapAlgorithm",
    ExecutionAlgorithmConfig(exec_algorithm_id=ExecAlgorithmId("TWAP")),
)

# %% [markdown]
# ## Run the backtest
#
# Call `.run()` to process all available data. The engine replays events in
# timestamp order with deterministic execution semantics.

# %%
# Run the engine (from start to end of data)
engine.run()

# %% [markdown]
# ## Post-run analysis
#
# The engine retains data and execution objects in memory for generating reports.
# It also logs a tearsheet with default statistics; see the
# [Portfolio statistics](../concepts/portfolio.md#portfolio-statistics) guide for
# custom statistics.

# %%
engine.generate_account_report(BINANCE)

# %%
engine.generate_order_fills_report()

# %%
engine.generate_positions_report()

# %% [markdown]
# ## Repeated runs
#
# Reset the engine for repeated runs. Instruments, data, and loaded components
# persist across resets; loaded components have their internal state reset.

# %%
# For repeated backtest runs, reset the engine
engine.reset()

# Clear or remove loaded components before adding replacements.

# %% [markdown]
# Remove and add individual components (actors, strategies, execution algorithms) as required.
#
# See the [BacktestEngine](../api_reference/backtest.md) API reference for the add and clear methods.
#

# %%
# Once done, good practice to dispose of the object if the script continues
engine.dispose()

40	@dataclass(frozen=True)
41	class ImportableFactoryConfig:
42	    """
43	    A factory import path in ``module:qualified_name`` form.
44	    """
45	
46	    path: str
47	
48	    def create(self) -> object:
49	        """
50	        Import and construct the configured factory.
51	        """
52	        return resolve_path(self.path)()
